articles.title: Introducing Firefox Enterprise | The Mozilla Blog
articles.summary:
Mozilla introduces Firefox Enterprise
Institutions are recalculating who controls the technology they rely on. Mozilla has an independent option to offer.
For years, organizations consolidated technology around a small number of providers to make things simpler. Fewer systems. Tighter integrations. More economies of scale. But that consolidation went well beyond technology. It consolidated dependency, too. The resulting risks have been debated, studied, and challenged along the way, but concentration continued. More work, data and critical infrastructure kept moving to the same few providers, while credible alternatives narrowed.
The deeper that dependency runs, the harder and more costly it becomes to change course. When something fails, changes or falls outside an institution’s control, that dependency becomes a risk for CIOs and CISOs to manage.
Nowhere are these stakes more visible than in Europe. Now institutions are re-assessing. Governments are pushing for greater digital autonomy, while regulated industries face growing pressure to find and manage their dependencies.
There’s a name for much of this debate about technological control: “sovereignty.”
What digital sovereignty means in practice varies. Across Europe, governments are investing in the security and resilience of critical IT infrastructure, reducing strategic dependencies and putting technological autonomy higher on national agendas. Different approaches, same underlying concern. Strip away the regional polic…

articles.title: Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Mixture-of-Experts kernel engineering on Amazon SageMaker AI
Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) is a sparsely-activated architecture that scales large language model (LLM) capacity while keeping per-token compute low. Because its operations account for a large share of total compute time, inefficiencies there directly raise request latency and cost. Therefore, optimizing MoE operations through kernel engineering offers the largest opportunity for performance gains.
Fused MoE is a key optimization technique for the MoE architecture. A fused MoE system merges token routing, data shuffling, and specialized network calculations into a single batched operation on the GPU. This replaces executing those routing and expert computations as separate, sequential loop operations. While this provides latency advantages, it also brings complexity in kernel implementations and debugging capability. High GPU utilization for this architecture requires hardware-specific optimizations.
In this post, we describe the different kernel optimizations we implemented for fused MoE models and show you how you can benefit from this work. We used a representative MoE model as our primary example.

articles.title: The UAE embraces AI for kindergartners
articles.summary:
In September, Henry Price observed a classroom of 7- to 8-year-olds learn about the Stone Age. They discussed and wrote about cave paintings, then put on virtual reality headsets to explore them.
The founding principal of Rugby School Dubai hopes his students will soon study ancient Egypt the same way — reading about it, creating artwork, and then stepping inside a virtual pyramid, or using artificial intelligence to “interview” a pharaoh.
“AI does not replace reading, writing, discussion, or creativity. It enhances them and opens new doors,” Price told Rest of World. “We want our students to be excited by AI, but never [be] passive users. We want children who use AI to ask better questions, not children who rely on it to give them all the answers.”
The United Arab Emirates recently became the first country to make AI a required K-12 subject.
That puts the country on one side of a growing global debate over what children should learn about AI and when they should encounter it. While the UAE and China are treating early AI literacy as a national priority, some Western governments are moving in the opposite direction. New York City introduced a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI in public schools from preschool through grade eight, citing concerns about children’s mental health. Norway has also enacted a similar near-ban for primary school children.

articles.title: SpaceX and Google both said no. Now his software is riding a SpaceX rocket next to Google’s | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The way Rama Afullo tells it, he saw orbital data centers coming.
The Kenyan American engineer previously worked in Google’s cloud computing business before a brief stint at SpaceX’s Starlink communications network in 2024. His experiences convinced him that there was untapped potential for computers in space.
“When I was at SpaceX, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no. When I was at Google, I tried to pitch this internally. They said no,” he tells TechCrunch.
So he left SpaceX and co-founded Satlyt, a new company with headquarters in Sunnyvale, California, and Nairobi, to build software for satellites that he hopes will let many satellites share the work of large computing jobs in space. The company has raised an $8 million seed round, Afullo exclusively told TechCrunch.
The timing looks good for him. SpaceX has since gone all-in on orbital data centers, and Satlyt’s software is set to launch Thursday on a SpaceX rocket alongside the first prototype for Google’s space data center effort, Project Suncatcher.
Unlike SpaceX, Google, or startups like Starcloud and Cowboy Space Company, Satlyt isn’t planning to build its own spacecraft. Afullo’s team is building the software to operate AI models on satellites, comparing his approach to VMware and Snowflake — companies whose platforms let users run complex software without worrying about the underlying infrastructure.

articles.title: Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down
articles.summary:
Rewinding the exponential: How we keep hardware usage down
More than 20% of the web sits behind Cloudflare’s network, and our team, the Data team, owns the data pipeline responsible for plumbing that data (and more) from our global network to applicable central data centers. The Cloudflare network is a globally distributed system supporting tens of thousands of servers. Data that power Cloudflare Logs, SQL API, observability, internal analytics, and more flow through this network and use our data pipeline to serve customers.
In May of this year, we were providing data delivery at roughly two billion events per second. This includes customer traffic as well as data sent from internal teams. Year after year, we tackle the same problem — exponential traffic growth against linear hardware growth. We have to react to this increase in order to keep resource costs under control. Over the past five years, we’ve made various improvements to compensate for the data volume increase in comparison to hardware allocation, equivalent to deferring two and a half years of hardware expansion. This post details those changes: breaking up our monolithic data schema in 2022, adjusting compression in 2024, rearchitecting pipeline replication in spring 2026, decentralizing sampling in summer 2026, and introducing aggregations into the pipeline in fall 2026.

articles.title: Under the hood, off the hot path: how D1 scales to millions of databases
articles.summary:
Under the hood, off the hot path: How D1 scales to millions of databases
Traditional database architecture assumes you have one or two big database clusters per application, usually accompanied by a connection pooling solution. AI-assisted development and vibe coding platforms turn this model inside out and are driving applications toward many small databases: one per user, application, preview environment, or tenant.
That model fits D1 particularly well. D1 is Cloudflare's managed, serverless database based on SQLite. It allows you to create millions of databases and only pay for what you use.
The question becomes: how do you scale the control plane for millions of databases without making every query slower by sending it through centralized bottlenecks?
We made a lot of architectural changes to scale out D1 to support platforms with millions of created databases, hundreds of thousands of which are active at any point.
This post is a behind-the-scenes deep dive into how the D1 control plane works. Many of the architectural patterns we will describe can be used by anyone building on top of Cloudflare’s Developer Platform. The post also gives a glimpse into how we build our own control planes.
Growth in numbers
There was already a steady growth in D1 usage when we started planning these changes, but we knew we would need to support a much bigger scale once large platforms started building with D1.

articles.title: Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Build long-horizon agents with Grok 4.7 on Amazon Bedrock
SpaceXAI’s Grok 4.7 is now available on Amazon Bedrock, which offers a choice of foundation models (FMs) from multiple providers. According to SpaceXAI, Grok 4.7 is trained to work longer on more difficult tasks and knows when to check its own work. That matters most for agents, which carry a task through many steps and must verify what they find along the way.
An agent that works this way has to do more than look things up. It has to form a candidate answer, check it against what it has learned, and refine it until it fits. Grok 4.7 exposes a reasoning effort setting that controls how much deliberation happens before each response, and for agent workloads a practical question is which level to run.
In this post, we build a tool-calling agent on Grok 4.7 and evaluate it on three tasks that require search rather than lookup. The tasks are diagnosing a two-service outage from its alerts, scheduling maintenance under interacting constraints, and choosing an optimal set of migrations under a budget. At least 78 of the flaws fixed this month are rated “critical,” meaning they could be exploited with little or no action by the user, and most of those critical bugs allow an attacker to execute code of their choice on the vulnerable system.
While Microsoft said there are no signs anyone is exploiting it yet, a security feature bypass in the .NET Framework (CVE-2026-108398) was publicly disclosed prior to today, potentially giving attackers advance time to work out how to exploit the bug.

articles.title: What’s old is new: Lightwell discovers novel zero-day vulnerability in core Java framework
articles.summary:
Enterprise IT runs on decades-old foundational code. The prevailing assumption around these mature components is that if code has been sitting untouched in production for ten years without breaking, it must be safe. Libraries like the Eclipse Implementation of Jakarta XML Binding (JAXB) quietly power enterprise applications in the background. Embedded deep into middleware stacks and application servers, they carry heavy workloads without drawing attention.
Advanced AI security tooling doesn’t ignore these deep-stack layers, however. It finds zero-day flaws hidden in structural parsing logic that standard static analysis tools miss entirely. And discovery is only part of the story. Any new vulnerabilities impacting these load-bearing pillars need to be discovered, analyzed, and swiftly addressed by the community. This is exactly what Lightwell did with a novel vulnerability within JAXB, identified as CVE-2026-92877.
Addressing novel flaws across the software lifecycle
When a vulnerability is discovered in a new framework, communities and maintainers respond quickly. The code is fresh, developers are actively tweaking it, and patches roll out quickly. Legacy components face a different reality. Unaddressed flaws in fundamental XML binding logic can compromise every application server, middleware pipeline, and cloud service that relies on it.

- Chained exploits: Isolated parsing bugs can be chained …

Diesel fuel powers everything from shipping to agriculture, and with prices hitting record highs in recent weeks, governments around the world are scrambling to contain the fallout.
For now, that’s meant releasing fuel from stockpiles, but in the coming years, the answer might be a new technology from an MIT startup called LNK Energies.
LNK has created a way to convert existing heavy-duty trucks from diesel to hydrogen, slashing pollution and costs while shielding operators from the price spikes that result from geopolitical instability like the war in Iran. “If you look at total cost of ownership of a Class 8 truck, it’s 13% cheaper than diesel,” Alexis Huynh, chief technology officer at LNK Energies, told TechCrunch. (Class 8 is the heaviest category of trucks, including big rigs.)
Automotive companies have been exploring the use of hydrogen in long-haul trucking in part because refilling a hydrogen tank is faster than recharging the massive batteries those trucks require. LNK’s approach is to carry hydrogen chemically attached to another compound. Liquid organic hydrogen carriers, or LOHCs, are liquids that can absorb and later release hydrogen, and they have been widely studied, but mostly for moving large quantities of hydrogen from refineries to fueling stations. Il avait tout fait seul : l’histoire, les images et la programmation.

Son nouveau jeu, Komiya en salle d’interrogatoire, a été créé avec Claude, l’IA d’Anthropic, et il en partage le lien. C’est une enquête en forme de visual novel, un genre de jeu narratif où l’histoire avance surtout par des dialogues, du texte et des illustrations, avec parfois des choix qui influencent le récit. Selon lui, il ne lui a fallu qu’une trentaine de minutes pour le créer.
Le joueur incarne un policier qui interroge Komiya, un ancien serrurier de 72 ans soupçonné d’avoir vidé le coffre d’un prêteur sur gages. Il ment, et il faut confronter ses déclarations aux preuves pour faire tomber son histoire. Deux jauges, « agitation » et « résistance », évoluent au fil des questions : si la résistance atteint 100, le suspect se mure dans le silence. articles.title: Pour refroidir l’iPhone Duo pliant, Apple fait passer un conduit de graphite dans sa charnière

Pour évacuer la chaleur de l’A20 Pro dans un appareil qui double d’épaisseur une fois plié, Apple a fait passer un conduit de graphite flexible à travers la charnière de l’iPhone Duo. Les ingénieurs de la marque détaillent cette pièce, qui relie les deux moitiés du pliant.
L’iPhone Duo, premier pliant d’Apple, doit gérer la chaleur d’une puce gravée en 2 nm dans un châssis en deux parties. Selon un entretien accordé par Apple à PCMag, la charnière joue ici un rôle thermique inattendu : elle sert de pont pour répartir la chaleur sur une plus grande surface.
Un conduit de graphite flexible traverse la charnière
Banafsheh Barabadi, responsable senior de la conception thermique chez Apple, qualifie ce point de « l’un des aspects techniquement les plus difficiles » du design. Le conduit transfère la chaleur d’une moitié de l’appareil à l’autre, ce qui augmente la surface disponible pour la dissiper. Sur un pliant, l’épaisseur double une fois l'appareil refermé, d’où l’intérêt de mettre les deux moitiés à contribution.
La pièce a dû être conçue conjointement par les équipes thermique et mécanique. Il s’agit d’un matériau flexible qui doit encaisser de très nombreux cycles d’ouverture tout en conservant sa conductivité thermique et son intégrité structurelle sur toute la vie du produit. Autrement dit, la même pièce doit être un bon conducteur et un bon ressort, deux qualités qui s’accordent rarement.

Even when artificial intelligence behaves exactly like a human, people are reluctant to consider it conscious, according to a new study from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (LMU).
As artificial intelligence becomes more advanced, reports of AI systems misleading users, working together, or appearing to pursue independent goals are becoming increasingly common. These behaviors often lead people to describe AI as though it can think, feel, or make decisions for itself. But does behaving like a human actually convince people that a machine has consciousness?
New research from LMU suggests that people make a clear distinction between displaying intelligent behavior and possessing a conscious mind, even when humans and AI act in precisely the same way.

Illustrating the pace of AI tool adoption within enterprises driving such fears, Shahar Bahat, CEO and co-founder of Pluto Security, says a newly announced AI tool can show up inside companies’ environment within a mere two hours of its release. articles.title: AI Turns Familiar Cyberattacks Into a Race Against Time
articles.summary:
In the AI era, phishing remains the top attack vector in both use (17% of breaches) and breach costs (averaging at $5.29 per breach) according to the IBM Cost of a Data Breach Report 2026. AI creates more personalized content for phishing with higher success rates. At the same time, AI can identify vulnerabilities, use the phished entry point and elevate privileges for lateral movement at greater speed.
None of this is new – cyberattacks haven’t changed with AI. “It just allows attackers to do the same familiar things much faster and at greater scale than ever before. The pressure comes from minimizing the time for defenders to respond,” says Steve Wallin, director of core integration and R&D labs leader at IBM UK.
For now, AI-generated attacks are still in the minority – little more than 20% of all attacks. But the writing (written by AI) is on the wall, and it is incumbent on enterprises to improve their security defenses now before the tsunami arrives in full.
SecurityWeek talked to Wallin on how enterprises should respond to this growing AI threat. Again, it is nothing new – it must just be done better.
It starts with a basic maxim that is as old as the ancient Delphic Oracle: ‘know thyself’. “Organizations must understand their existing security posture. The key to defending against this increasing volume of attacks and decreasing time to respond is again nothing new. It means focusing on proactive rather than reactive defense. It is security by design from the ground up…

Entre 1780 y 1840, la producción por trabajador en Gran Bretaña creció un 46 % (estimación de Nicholas Crafts y Knick Harley) y el salario real un 12 % (la de Charles Feinstein).
El historiador económico Robert Allen bautizó ese periodo como la "pausa de Engels", por Friedrich Engels, que describió la situación de la clase obrera inglesa en 1845. Según su estudio de 2009, la tasa de beneficio de los empresarios se duplicó mientras los sueldos casi no se movían, y solo hacia mediados del siglo XIX los salarios alcanzaron a la productividad: entre 1840 y 1900, la producción por trabajador aumentó un 90 % y el salario real un 123 %. Allen lo atribuye a la acumulación de capital, que tardó en ponerse a la altura del progreso técnico.

articles.title: High-speed video reveals how honey bee stingers pump venom
articles.summary:
Honey bees are known to leave their stingers embedded in tender flesh once they sting you and fly away. Scientists have now determined that the stinger is able to continue pumping venom into its unfortunate victim even after the bee flies away, thanks to a unique double-piston pump-like mechanism, according to a new paper published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.
Different species have evolved different mechanisms for delivering venom, which involves piercing the skin and then pumping venom from a gland or reservoir. Spiders, for instance, have muscles surrounding their venom glands, which contract and eject venom through hollow fangs. Bees, wasps, and ants deliver venom via their stingers, either by contracting muscles around the venom reservoir or through stiff elements called lancets working together to pump venom.
Honey bees (Apis mellifera) add a unique feature: Worker bees fly away after inserting their stingers in the target, leaving the stinger behind. The stinger continues to penetrate the tissue and pump venom on its own, a rare phenomenon known as autotomy. A honey bee’s stinger has three main interlocking elements that form the venom canal: a stylet that widens to form the main pumping chamber and two sharp-tipped lancets that slide back and forth, piercing the tissue and pumping venom into the target. But the precise mechanism by which the pumping action is achieved has never been directly observed.

articles.title: Cloudflare’s OHTTP Gateway Refuses to Decrypt Requests That Arrive through Cloudflare
articles.summary:
Cloudflare has opened a closed beta of the Cloudflare OHTTP Gateway, a managed endpoint that decrypts Oblivious HTTP requests on an origin’s behalf. The design decision that drew most of the attention is a refusal rather than a feature: the Gateway will not decrypt requests that reach it from Cloudflare Workers or from hosts proxied through Cloudflare.
Oblivious HTTP, standardized as RFC 9458, splits a request across two parties. The client encrypts the inner HTTP request to the gateway’s public key using HPKE and sends the sealed payload to a relay. The relay sees the client’s IP address but cannot read the request. The gateway decrypts it and forwards plain HTTP to the application, so it sees the contents but only ever sees the relay’s address.
That only works if different operators run the two hops. Putting a Worker in front of the Gateway, or proxying the relay through Cloudflare, would route the client-identifying hop and the decryption hop through the same company, so Cloudflare built a product that declines to run in that configuration. Authors Lara Schull and Akshat Mahajan write that the model "requires that the relay and app server be operated by separate, non-colluding parties."
For a team evaluating this, the practical cost is the relay. Cloudflare does not supply one for the Gateway, and says the component is not the hard part, since relays "can run on any infrastructure provider, and they’re simple." The hard part is being in a position to "verifiably promise to…

Rockets are, infamously, a real pain in the butt. Our old friend physics forces rockets to be built with almost no room for error, and even then only a small fraction of their weight makes it to orbit.

The malware’s developers have been constantly updating its codebase and adding new functionality, and the threat has remained highly active, with Netskope observing over 1,200 incidents across 100 organizations during the third quarter of the year.

AWS has introduced an enhanced Custom Event Bus for Amazon EventBridge, targeting a problem that often emerges when event-driven architectures move beyond a single team or AWS account: the event infrastructure itself becomes fragmented. The new model allows organisations to create a single event bus shared across multiple AWS accounts, while adding native event ordering, retention and replay, content-based deduplication, simplified subscriptions and a new pricing model.
The change addresses an architectural tension in enterprise AWS environments. Organisations commonly use multiple accounts to provide isolation between teams and applications, but this can lead to EventBridge buses being connected through cross-account rules and forwarding configurations. As the number of consumers grows, the resulting topology becomes harder to govern and understand, while forwarding the same event through multiple buses can introduce additional processing and routing costs. AWS's new model instead positions a central bus as an organisational event backbone, with individual teams managing their own subscriptions.
The enhanced Custom Event Bus can be shared across AWS accounts using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM). A platform team can therefore establish a central event bus while allowing application teams to publish and subscribe from their own accounts. Zwar begrüßen die Banken, dass Kunden sich künftig per Wallet geldwäscherechtlich identifizieren können, wenn sie ein Konto eröffnen. Die Institute fordern jedoch, klar festzulegen, dass es ausreicht, die vom Wallet–Verfahren bereitgestellten Daten zu speichern, also dass eine Ausweiskopie weder erforderlich noch technisch umsetzbar ist. Ohne diese Präzisierung könnten Banken sonst vorsichtshalber zusätzliche Nachweise verlangen, wodurch der Vorteil einer schnellen, papierlosen Kontoeröffnung verloren gehen könnte.
Außerdem müsse das Gesetz klarer regeln, wann Banken eine fremde Wallet akzeptieren müssen, wer bei technischen Fehlern haftet und welche Daten ihnen zur Betrugsabwehr zur Verfügung stehen.

The underlying identity tactics are largely unchanged: attackers still compromise identities, reuse credentials, escalate privileges and misuse legitimate access. The threat is that AI makes familiar techniques cheaper and easier to run at scale.

articles.title: Small AI Models Could Soon Self-Replicate on IoT Devices, Anthropic Warns
articles.summary:
Small AI models may be only months away from being able to self-replicate across commercial IoT devices, without needing a data center, according to research from Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team.
The study looks at AI worms that run their own model directly on the devices they compromise. Such malware would be hard to shut down because it has no central point to switch off, though it would likely spread slowly.
The researchers bought 15 off-brand Android-based TV boxes for about $55 each. A 26-billion-parameter open-weight model split across them ran at 0.39 tokens per second.
Rather than exploitation, which prior studies have already examined, the team focused on whether models could get AI inference running on unfamiliar hardware. A 9-billion-parameter model did so on eight of the nine hardware types tested.
The researchers then tested the full replication cycle on a closed network of eight emulated Android devices, with the hacking step deliberately kept trivial. Of the open-weight models tested, only GLM-5.2 completed it, reaching all eight devices in four of five runs.
Anthropic considers the results an upper bound for real-world success, but notes that past IoT botnets such as Mirai spread simply by trying default manufacturer credentials.
Models with 30 billion parameters or fewer can already complete many of the individual steps but make mistakes when chaining them together. If they keep improving at their historical rate, Anthropic expects them to reach GLM-5.2’s level…

articles.title: Docker Hub flaw let attackers impersonate users, tamper with images
articles.summary:
Docker has disclosed a critical vulnerability (CVE-2026-105445) in Docker Hub that let attackers access another user’s container repositories using a personal access token (PAT).
Docker Hub is an online registry for storing, sharing, and downloading container images - templates that package everything needed for an application to run in an isolated environment.
In Docker Hub, a PAT serves as a secret used to authenticate tools and workflows. It allows you to pull, push, or delete container images.
According to a security bulletin from the Docker team, an attacker could create an account and PAT, then convert the account into an organization and name a target user as its owner.
The CVE-2026-105445 flaw stems from Docker Hub reassigning a personal access token (PAT) to a designated organization owner without changing its secret or obtaining the target's consent. This allowed the attacker to use the token to authenticate as the target.
Depending on the token’s scope and the target’s permissions, attackers could pull, push, or delete images in the target’s repositories and accessible organizations.
“Within the scope of the token, a re-assigned PAT acted as the target user at the registry level, meaning an attacker could potentially pull, push, and/or delete images in the target’s repositories and in organizations where the target had access,” Docker explained.

The sale was brokered by a company called SimpleClosure, part of a new growth sector in tech: businesses catering to dying startups. articles.title: Agentic AI Automates RTL Waveform Analysis And Debugging (Columbia, Google)
articles.summary:
Researchers at Columbia University, Google DeepMind, and Google published a technical paper titled “Back to the Future: Rethinking EDA Infrastructure for Agentic Systems in Chip Design Verification.”
Abstract
“The unprecedented computational scale of modern artificial intelligence depends on complex, multi-billion-transistor Systems-on-Chip, yet the workflows that verify these chips remain stubbornly manual. Although Large Language Models (LLMs) have made rapid inroads into Electronic Design Automation (EDA), approximately 74.6% of existing studies target static Register-Transfer Level (RTL) code generation, leaving post-simulation verification and interactive waveform debugging largely untouched. We introduce Back-to-the-Future (BTTF), an end-to-end agentic framework that closes this infrastructural gap. BTTF distills massive, unstructured simulation dumps into a normalized relational SQLite database and couples it with a collaborative multi-agent orchestration engine that translates natural-language verification queries into schema-aware SQL while correlating signal anomalies with versioned RTL repositories. Across a 150-query benchmark, BTTF attains 95.33% execution accuracy, charting a practical path toward autonomous EDA verification.”
Find the technical paper here. October 2026.

articles.title: Jonathan es una tortuga, tiene 194 años y acabamos de descubrir por qué su ADN envejece tan lentamente

El secreto de la longevidad extrema siempre ha sido un tema que ha fascinado a la ciencia, pero para saber cómo se puede vivir más de 200 años, a veces no hay que mirar a los humanos, sino a un apacible reptil que lleva caminando por este planeta desde antes que se inventara la bombilla, como es Jonathan. Esta es una tortuga gigante que, a sus 194 años, ostenta el récord de ser el animal terrestre más longevo del mundo.
Su razón. Aguantar durante todos los años hace que la gente busque el porqué. Y aquí la ciencia ha decidido asomarse al interior de sus células gracias a un equipo internacional que ha secuenciado su genoma y su metiloma para entender la razón por la que Jonathan no envejece como el resto de animales.
Un simple frotis. Para entender un poco mejor a Jonathan, no hizo falta someterle a dolorosas pruebas, sino que solo bastó con raspar la mucosa bucal del animal. A partir de esta muestra, un equipo internacional comparó su ADN con el de otras tortugas gigantes de Aldabra mucho más jóvenes.
El resultado. Lo que encontraron en el código genético fue un arsenal biológico muy importante, puesto que se pudieron identificar hasta 287 genes con variantes exclusivas de Jonathan. Pero lo interesante es que muchas de estas variantes están íntimamente ligadas a la supresión de tumores y a la reparación del ADN.

The agent did the work. The audit log couldn’t say who asked.
More than 20 percent of the MCP-related access policies that Shawn Petty’s team reviewed across customer and prospect environments were broken or missing, according to a recent account published in The New Stack. In most cases, the MCP server ran on someone’s personal token rather than a service account.
At 12 p.m. Eastern/9 a.m. Pacific on Tuesday, October 27, Petty, Chief Customer Officer at CloudBolt, and Mike Bombard, Director of Global Pre-Sales Engineering at CloudBolt, will join The New Stack host Viktor Farcic for a live demo of how to trace an agent’s actions back to the person responsible for them.
You have successfully registered for the webinar.
The problem, though, usually shows up after an incident: That personal token puts an engineer’s name into the audit trail for everything the agent did. Meanwhile, a shared service account puts the account’s name there instead. In both cases, the audit trail isn’t able to identify who precisely asked the agent to do the work or who approved the access it used.
Access that goes through a request, approval, and grant in the identity provider is provisioned, and the identity provider records it. Access that an agent picks up along the way is emergent: A role inherited from the service that launched it, or a developer’s own token lent out to finish a task. Ein internationales Forschungsteam hat das bislang am weitesten entfernte Radiosignal der Astronomiegeschichte aufgezeichnet. Der als Fast Radio Burst bekannte Ausbruch reiste mehr als zehn Milliarden Jahre durch das Weltall, bevor er die Erde erreichte und von den Instrumenten der Wissenschaftler:innen verarbeitet werden konnte.
Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, entstand das Signal mit der Bezeichnung FRB 20240304B, als das Universum erst etwa drei Milliarden Jahre alt war. Die initiale Aufzeichnung gelang zunächst mit dem Radioteleskop MeerKAT in der südafrikanischen Provinz Nordkap, das für derartige Himmelsdurchmusterungen konstruiert wurde.
James-Webb-Teleskop lokalisiert den Ursprung
Um den Ursprungsort zu bestimmen, nutzten die Astronom:innen im Nachgang das James-Webb-Weltraumteleskop der US-Raumfahrtbehörde Nasa. Dessen Infrarotinstrumente zeigten bei der Analyse, dass der Ausbruch aus einer sehr kleinen Galaxie stammt, die aktuell in hoher Geschwindigkeit neue Sterne bildet.
Diese Galaxie weist im direkten Vergleich zu unserer Milchstraße nur einen geringen Anteil an schweren Elementen auf. Der Astronom Themiya Nanayakkara von der Universität Sydney im australischen Bundesstaat New South Wales erklärte gegenüber The Guardian, dass zum Zeitpunkt der Signalentstehung weder die Erde noch die Sonne existierten.

San Francisco-based startup Niobia is betting big on a critical but often overlooked part of battery and chip making: helping engineers understand how and why things go wrong. Its AI software flags production defects and lets engineers ask a chatbot what caused them, aiming to deliver answers in minutes rather than days.
How it works (broadly): The company’s customers place AI agents on their production lines to look for defects, then loop in human engineers to work out what might cause a product to fail. The agents run on self-contained GPUs mounted directly on manufacturing equipment, much like a sensor. They can spot pinhole-sized flaws such as scratches. Niobia’s AI also gathers all the data in one place so engineers can ask a chatbot what went wrong and dig deeper into the cause.
Speed is so critical because chips and batteries are some of the world’s most important products, while also increasingly in short supply. As manufacturers continue to develop and improve their technologies, things inevitably go awry during research and development. Engineers then spend days or longer figuring out a fix before they can restart production. Each flaw or mistake can prove costly — sometimes running into the millions of dollars — and set back manufacturing timelines.

AI has been changing the pace and profile of vulnerability discovery, and the tech giant has been adjusting its bug bounty programs in recent months.

At the time it announced a base reward of $500 for memory safety issues, with multipliers for reachability and the level of exploitability.
The company is now quadrupling base rates for memory safety flaws, to $2,000. Despite the increase, the new rates remain well below those offered before the April overhaul.
Vulnerabilities in Chrome’s browser, GPU and network processes can now earn researchers up to $20,000. In the case of the renderer process, bug bounty hunters can receive up to $8,000 for use-after-free and memory write bugs.
V8 sandbox vulnerabilities are moving to a flat rate of $5,000, while V8 logic bugs will be rewarded with $4,000.
As for issues not related to memory safety, medium-severity flaws will be rewarded with $2,000 if the vulnerability report includes or directly leads to an identified fix. Sandbox escapes not involving memory safety bugs can get bug bounties of up to $20,000.
Google is also reintroducing a $2,000 fuzzer bonus for developing novel fuzzers.

In a nutshell: PC builders have long tried to find the most optimal cooling setups for their components, moving around fans, cables, etc. to find the best configurations. A YouTube channel decided to try something a little different: moving the components themselves. This included shifting the GPU next to a case's side-intake, which resulted in a 17-degree drop in temperatures.
The experiment was carried out by TrashBench, which used an Asus ROG Strix RTX 3080 inside a dual-chamber case. The cooling came from three side-intake fans, a rear exhaust, and a top-mounted 360mm CPU AIO.
The idea was to change component placement without moving the case fans. PCIe riser cables were used so the graphics card could be moved away from its usual slot on the motherboard.
Testing involved looping 3DMark Time Spy alongside 7-Zip running on 12 CPU threads. All fans stayed at fixed RPMs, with each configuration tested for ten minutes and temperatures averaged over the final five.
The GPU's first position was on the case floor, which required the removal of the bottom mesh because it touched the card's fans. GPU temperatures barely changed, but the CPU and motherboard VRM dropped around 4°C and 7°C, respectively. Conventional vertical mounting slightly worsened GPU temperatures while modestly improving everything else.

Avec son écran HomeView (299 $, environ 265 € hors taxes), officialisé ce mardi 13 octobre après plusieurs mois de rumeurs, Apple entend devenir un acteur majeur du marché de la domotique. Il y a néanmoins un frein à son ambition : le catalogue de la multinationale est limité, alors que l’idée est bien de piloter un maximum de choses chez soi. Voilà pourquoi Apple a annoncé ce qu’il appelle l’Apple Home Collection, une gamme de produits conçus par des tiers pour une expérience complète.
Apple n’a pas choisi n’importe qui : LG, qui lui a déjà fourni des écrans pour Mac (les UltraFine 4K et 5K) quand le Studio Display n’existait pas encore, et Schneider Electric (cocorico). La stratégie est simple à comprendre. Quand un client Apple ira chercher son HomeView en Apple Store, il pourra repartir avec des accessoires 100 % compatibles et parfaitement intégrés à l’écosystème Maison. « Il suffit d’un simple toucher avec votre iPhone, et tout est géré depuis l’application Maison d’Apple – aucune application ni aucun compte séparé n’est nécessaire », indique Apple.
LG et Schneider, partenaires domestiques d’Apple
Des sonnettes, caméras ou thermostats compatibles avec l’application Maison existent déjà par milliers chez d’autres marques, grâce aux certifications Works with Apple Home et Matter. articles.title: Gemini 4 Argon debuts with a unified 1M input/output token limit
articles.summary:
Gemini 4 Argon debuts with a unified 1M input/output token limit
On Tuesday, Google made Gemini 4 Argon, the company’s new flagship model, available to developers on the paid tier of the Gemini API through Google AI Studio, as well as in several of the company’s other developer and consumer tools.
Google announced the model on September 30. Initial external access was limited to selected cyber defenders in its Fairwind Program and other trusted testers; Google employees were also using it internally.
Gemini 4 Argon pricing
Google is giving the model a competitive price. Developers will pay an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens through November 30, with a single 1 million-token budget for input and output combined. That’s the same price as OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol.
After that date, Google’s new model will cost $4 and $20 per million tokens, matching Anthropic’s Claude Opus 5.5. Cached input tokens are 95 percent off during the introductory period.
During the introductory period, Argon also costs a fifth of what Anthropic charges for Claude Fable 5.1 and OpenAI charges for GPT-6 Astra, which both list at $10 and $50 per million tokens.
Developers can call the model as gemini-4-argon through Google’s Interactions API, with support in the google-genai SDKs. Android developers can also build it into their apps through Firebase AI Logic.

À ne pas confondre avec l'astuce de la pièce de monnaie posée sur la box, qui relève du pur mythe : ici, une équipe de chercheurs du département d'informatique de Dartmouth College a démontré en 2017 que l'aluminium, correctement positionné derrière un routeur, fonctionne comme un réflecteur parabolique capable de rediriger les ondes radio vers une zone ciblée.
	
Avec un investissement d'environ 35 dollars et en définissant les besoins de couverture, on peut fabriquer un réflecteur sur mesure qui surpasse des antennes coûtant plusieurs milliers de dollars.

articles.title: TFG London cyberattack disrupts systems at Hobbs and Whistles retailers
articles.summary:
TFG London detected a cybersecurity incident that impacted IT systems used by the Phase Eight, Hobbs, and Whistles premium fashion brands.
The company disclosed earlier today that several IT systems remain unavailable, although physical stores remain open for customers.
According to the press release, the incident has not affected the group’s other brands, Inside Story and White Stuff, or its operations in Australia and Africa.
TFG London is the UK subsidiary of South Africa’s The Foschini Group, which owns the aforementioned five fashion and homeware brands.
As of mid-2026, the group operated 649 retail locations globally and reported annual sales of £488 million ($646M).
The company said it detected the cyberattack on October 11 and immediately activated its incident response and business continuity plans, bringing in external cybersecurity experts to help contain the threat.
TFG London is investigating whether any customer information has been compromised, and says it will notify affected individuals or organizations if it data has been affected.
BleepingComputer could not find any threat actor publicly claiming the TFG London breach.
The incident at TFG London comes shortly after another UK fashion retailer, ASOS, suffered a data breach after hackers sent push notifications to users of its mobile app.

AI causes uproar in mathematics as experts warn against sharing research with LLMs after OpenAI shares 722 manuscripts and proofs — professor argues that the field must focus on building community over raw solutions
Mathematics is a collaborative field, now disrupted by AI
Last week, OpenAI shared over 400 results for longstanding mathematical formulas that have troubled humans for decades; now researchers say it could take years for humans to validate and prove all the AI-driven work. But while analysts try to check the work of the unnamed OpenAI internal frontier model that found these alleged solutions, mathematicians argue this kind of AI-powered research and release threatens the field itself.
There's even the claim that by leaping from a prompt to a solution without a clear working in between, there is little benefit to these solutions in the first place. Mathematicians and the field itself may not be able to build on the results, as they don't know how they were achieved, nor has the development of such solutions produced new fields of mathematical understanding.
To make matters worse, there are suggestions that the growing confluence of mathematical and cybersecurity capabilities of frontier AI could bring into question the sanctity of cryptography itself. Alongside raising serious concerns for national security and modern digital systems, it could also put trillions of dollars worth of cryptocurrency at imminent risk.

articles.title: Licube wants to be the fuel provider to the fusion power industry — see how at TechCrunch Disrupt | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
If fusion power pans out, and there are signs that it will, the world will need a lot more lithium.
That’s the bet behind Licube, a startup that has licensed technology from Hirosaki University in Japan, to purify lithium-6, the form of lithium that fusion plants need to make their own fuel, out of naturally occurring lithium.
The reason comes down to the fuel supply. A lot of things have to go right for fusion power to hit the grid, and one of them is the fuel. Most planned plants would run on a mix of two fuels, deuterium and tritium. Deuterium is easy to come by, but tritium is extremely rare in nature, and it’s an open secret in the fusion world that there isn’t enough of it to power every planned plant.
The proposed workaround is to make tritium on site, inside the power plant itself. A fusion reaction gives off a stream of fast-moving particles called neutrons. Startups plan to surround the reactor with a blanket of lithium, so that when a neutron strikes a lithium atom, the atom splits into helium and tritium. The tritium can then be collected, purified, and fed back into the reactor as fuel.
Not all lithium does this job equally well. It comes in two slightly different forms, lithium-6 and lithium-7, named for their weights. Lithium-6 is far better at capturing neutrons and producing tritium, but it makes up only about 7.5% of natural lithium, and the rest is the heavier lithium-7. Tras meses de retrasos y de ceder terreno a Anthropic y OpenAI, el gigante tecnológico contraataca con una nueva IA enfocada en flujos de trabajo completos. Gemini 4 llega con mejoras en razonamiento, programación y tareas de larga duración.
Si bien Google ya había anunciado Gemini 4 Argon a finales de septiembre, el modelo no se encontraba disponible. La tecnológica lo ofreció primero a un grupo de socios especializados en ciberseguridad para evaluarlo. La buena noticia es que el modelo de Google ya se puede usar en la app de Gemini.
De acuerdo con Google, Gemini 4 Argon está diseñado para proyectos de ingeniería de software, conocimiento empresarial en áreas como derecho y finanzas, así como también en defensa en ciberseguridad. La compañía coloca a esta versión como el comienzo de la próxima era de su inteligencia de frontera, un modelo que tendrá lo suficiente para medirse con Claude, ChatGPT y otras IA poderosas.
El cambio más notable con respecto a la versión anterior es que Argon responde de forma más directa y con menos titubeos. Gemino 4 dejará atrás los clichés y las respuestas con muchas repeticiones que no llevan a ningún lado, algo que veíamos en la generación anterior. articles.title: The Paris Auto Show is full of interesting cars Americans can’t have
articles.summary:
Perhaps the days when auto shows debuted new models aren’t entirely over. The big trade shows for cars were a gateway drug for many, expos where you could see the newest models of today and the concepts of tomorrow. But automakers increasingly got tired of sharing the spotlight with each other. New reveals moved offsite to events the night or even the week before the show itself. One by one, brands pulled out of auto show after auto show until there was little left to see. And then the pandemic hit.
But the news out of Paris, where its auto show held media day yesterday, seems like we stepped back into a time when automakers would debut new cars aplenty. That retro vibe extends to the cars themselves, with plenty of familiar nameplates reimagined.
France’s Renault has a long and glorious history of delightful concept cars, and more on what it brought to Paris later. But the star of the show was arguably Stellantis, with strong work from Citroen, Peugeot, and Fiat, to name but three. But this article is meant to irritate you, because I’m pretty sure none of the stuff you’re seeing here will come to the United States. And it’s doubly irritating considering what Stellantis’ brands do offer us over here, doubling down on the same malign trends I saw back in 2020: did you know they’re about to relaunch a V8 Hellcat-powered Charger?

articles.title: Backstage 1.55 Adds Scaffolder Task Recovery and Removes Deprecated Catalog APIs
articles.summary:
The Backstage project has released version 1.55 of its open-source developer portal framework, adding automatic recovery for Software Template tasks that crash or time out. The release also removes a set of deprecated catalog APIs and moves the search module to Elasticsearch 8, so platform teams have several breaking changes to work through before they upgrade.
Task recovery sits behind a new scaffolder.taskRecovery configuration section. When it is enabled, the scaffolder resumes a task from the last completed step, keeps task secrets until the task reaches a terminal state and persists completed step outputs so later steps can read them. The release notes warn that actions used by recovered tasks should be idempotent or use checkpoints, because a resumed task can run an action a second time. The new section replaces three experimental flags, which still work as fallbacks.
The feature responds to a long-standing request. In April 2025, on a GitHub issue tracking scaffolder task retries, Manoj Azad wrote, "Currently, having to re-run the entire scaffolder process can be not only inconvenient but also problematic from a technical standpoint." The 1.55 feature covers tasks interrupted by a crash or time-out, which addresses part of that request.

articles.title: Shareholder revolt leaves Africa Bitcoin Corporation with two directors

Africa Bitcoin Corporation (ABC), South Africa’s listed Bitcoin treasury firm and financial services group, faces a new battle over who joins its board after four directors, including its chairperson and interim chief executive, resigned following a shareholder push to remove them.
With just two directors remaining, the company must rebuild its board while a separate demand to appoint two new non-executive directors remains unresolved.
The dispute centres on two shareholder demands. Investors holding approximately 76% of ABC’s shares called for the appointment of two new non-executive directors, a move the board opposed on governance grounds. A subsequent demand, backed by shareholders holding approximately 71.8% of the company’s shares, sought the removal of four existing directors.
All four have since resigned, making the removal resolutions unnecessary, but the original demand for two new appointments remains in force.
ABC now faces a governance test at a critical point in its transformation from a small-business financier into a Bitcoin treasury company. Shareholders have forced out most of its board, but the fight over who should replace them remains unsettled, raising questions about how the company will balance investor control, regulatory scrutiny, and independent oversight as it pursues its new strategy.

articles.title: Jusqu’à 4 500 € de remise immédiate : on a déniché les meilleures promos du Mondial de l’Auto pour acheter votre voiture électrique au meilleur prix — Frandroid

Les visiteurs profitent de décors somptueux, d’animations, de concept-cars assez fous et de modèles de voitures fraîchement commercialisés.

Meta ha lanzado este lunes Muse Wonder y Muse Wonder Full, los primeros modelos de sus “Superintelligence Labs” que, según la compañía, se colocan a la vanguardia junto con los mejores modelos de OpenAI y Anthropic. Llegan en un momento en que Meta intenta demostrar que toda la oleada de despidos y la profunda reestructuración de su división de IA, puesta en marcha el año pasado, está dando sus frutos.
Muy atrás. Meta se quedó atrás en la carrera de la IA después del fiasco de Llama 4 el año pasado. Desde entonces, sus rivales han avanzado con sistemas mucho más capaces. Mark Zuckerberg respondió creando Meta Superintelligence Labs y contratando a Alexandr Wang, el exdirector ejecutivo de Scale AI, y uno de los nombres propios más destacados de la IA, para liderarlo.
Muse Wonder es la primera prueba real de si esa apuesta ha funcionado. De momento, si hablamos en términos económicos, los inversores han reaccionado positivamente. Y es que según Bloomberg, las acciones de Meta subieron hasta un 4,7 % tras la noticia.
Qué hay de nuevo. Hay dos modelos. Muse Wonder será pronto el cerebro de Muse, la app de agentes de IA personales de Meta, para los suscriptores de los niveles mensuales de 20 y 100 dólares. Por otro lado está Muse Wonder Full, que se trata de la versión más potente y estará limitada a los suscriptores de Muse Code, la herramienta de programación de IA de Meta. De momento ésta no se ofrecerá a través de la API.

articles.title: Endeavor Catalyst closes $320m Fund V - Disrupt Africa
articles.summary:
Endeavor Catalyst, the venture capital arm of global entrepreneur network Endeavor, has closed its oversubscribed Fund V at US$320 million, taking its total assets under management past US$850 million.
Endeavor Catalyst invests exclusively in companies led by Endeavor Entrepreneurs, co-investing alongside leading venture capital and growth equity firms. Across its five funds, it has already backed 437 companies in 44 markets, deploying more than US$500 million across 469 investments.
Africa makes up seven per cent of both the portfolio and Catalyst capital, with 29 companies backed across five African markets, including the likes of Flutterwave, Moniepoint, MAX and Moove. Six of these are valued at US$1 billion or more. A decade ago, the fund had made no African investments.
Fund V has already backed 30 companies and deployed more than US$55 million, with a further US$25 million to US$30 million expected to be invested before the end of 2026.
“For the founders we have yet to welcome into the Endeavor community, it sends an important signal: world-class capital is looking for ambition, wherever that ambition is being built,” said Ireayo Oladunjoye, managing director and CEO of Endeavor Nigeria.

articles.title: Rätsel der Monsterwellen gelöst: Wie KI die Gefahr auf See berechenbar macht
articles.summary:
Formel statt Seemannsgarn: KI analysiert die Entstehung von Monsterwellen
Am 17. November 2020 registrierte eine Sensorboje des kanadischen Unternehmens MarineLabs eine Wassersäule, die Ozeanograf:innen weltweit beschäftigte. Das im Pazifik vor der Küste von Ucluelet verankerte Messgerät zeichnete eine Einzelwelle von 17,6 Metern Höhe auf. Das Ereignis sticht deshalb heraus, weil der restliche Seegang zu diesem Zeitpunkt bei lediglich rund sechs Metern lag.
Damit ein solches Ereignis in der Wissenschaft als Monsterwelle (im Fachjargon Rogue Wave genannt) eingestuft wird, ist nicht die absolute Höhe entscheidend, sondern das Verhältnis zur sogenannten signifikanten Wellenhöhe. Dieser Referenzwert beschreibt die Durchschnittshöhe des höchsten Drittels aller Wellen in einem Messzeitraum. Übertrifft eine einzelne Welle diesen Durchschnitt um mehr als das Doppelte gilt sie als Monsterwelle.
Mit dem fast Dreifachen der signifikanten Wellenhöhe ist das Ereignis von Ucluelet proportional die extremste jemals gemessene Welle. Zum Vergleich: Die berühmte Draupner-Welle, die am 1. Januar 1995 an einer norwegischen Ölplattform in der Nordsee den ersten Beweis für die Existenz des Phänomens lieferte, war zwar 25,6 Meter hoch, trat aber in einem schweren Seegang von ohnehin schon zwölf Metern auf.
Warum etablierte Erklärungsmodelle auf dem Ozean versagen

India should look to China for lessons on building technological capabilities rather than continue relying on a model centred on providing software services to global companies, Zoho Co-founder and Chief Scientist Sridhar Vembu said on Tuesday.

articles.title: Exclusive: Cambridge Heavy Industries has been quietly building a desktop fusion device | TechCrunch

Fusion power usually conjures images of massive industrial facilities laced with large lasers or magnets, but a startup in Cambridge, Massachusetts, has been quietly building a device that can fit on a tabletop.
The optics of the device were on display behind Yun Kai, co-founder and CEO of Cambridge Heavy Industries, while he chatted with me on a video call. The company has been operating in stealth out of a small lab near MIT, and Kai gave TechCrunch an exclusive look at the technology it has been developing.
“We purposely built a small modular reactor. It’s tiny, it’s benchtop,” he told me. “Because it’s small, it makes everything easier.”
The small size has allowed Cambridge Heavy to experiment and iterate quickly. “The small module nature can enable 50 to 80 experiments, 50 to 80 shots per day,” he said. Data from those experiments will feed simulations that use AI to optimize the design.
That nimble approach has attracted investor attention. The startup recently raised a $6.2 million seed round led by Azolla Ventures with participation from Overlay, Neta Foundation, P3A, MassCEC, and the Rothrock family.
Cambridge Heavy’s fusion reactor uses lasers to compress a fuel target, similar to the groundbreaking experiment that proved controlled fusion reactions could produce more power than they consume. But unlike other inertial confinement designs, Cambridge Heavy’s minimizes the number of lasers required to spark fusion.

articles.title: Skydance’s Discovery+ prices increase by up to 20 percent
articles.summary:
Discovery+ subscription prices went up today.
Ad-free plans for new subscribers went from $10 per month to $12/month. Ad-based plans went from $6 to $7.
The new prices take effect for new subscribers immediately. Current subscribers to the streaming service, which primarily features unscripted content, like reality shows and documentaries, will receive 30 days’ notice before the new prices take effect, starting with bills issued as of November 12.
The higher prices come a week after Paramount Skydance bought Discovery+ parent company Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD), forming Skydance.
However, a Skydance spokesperson told Ars Technica that the pricing changes were in the works before Discovery+ knew about the merger’s closing date and were not planned in anticipation of a merger.
The spokesperson said that Discovery+’s prices are regularly evaluated to ensure that they are in line with the content and experience that the service offers, and the new prices reflect that.
Discovery+ has increased its prices three times since launching in 2012. Before today, the most recent price hike occurred in January 2025, when ad-based monthly subscriptions increased from $5 to $6, and ad-free plans went from $9 to $10.

articles.title: Ivanti Zero-Day Chain Gave Attackers Root Access to Fully Patched VPN
articles.summary:
Ivanti on Tuesday warned customers that a zero-day vulnerability in its Connect Secure (ICS) VPN appliances has been exploited in the wild.
Tracked as CVE-2026-104935 and rated high severity, the issue is an authentication bypass that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary commands. Ivanti says it’s aware of exploitation affecting a limited number of customers.
Volexity discovered the in-the-wild exploitation while investigating an incident at one of its customers. A previously undocumented threat actor it tracks as UTA0576 had chained three zero-days to gain unauthenticated, root-level code execution on a fully patched ICS appliance.
According to Volexity, CVE-2026-104935 covers two of the flaws: an authentication bypass and a remote code execution bug. Ivanti has patched these vulnerabilities with the release of ICS versions 22.8R2.5, 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.0, and 25.1.3.1.
The third vulnerability, a privilege escalation issue, remains unpatched, and the vendor plans to fix it over the coming weeks.
Volexity, which found evidence of exploitation starting on October 3, says UTA0576 focused primarily on credential theft, data exfiltration, network reconnaissance, and log tampering.
The attackers stole domain credentials stored on the appliance and exfiltrated limited Active Directory metadata. Using a custom tool, they searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys.

articles.title: Anthropic’s red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes. Then the math got unsettling.
articles.summary:
Anthropic’s red team ran AI on 15 cheap TV boxes. Then the math got unsettling.
For roughly $825, Anthropic’s Frontier Red Team built a cluster of 15 off-brand Android TV boxes that runs an AI model at 0.39 tokens per second, painfully slow for a chatbot but fine for software with nowhere to be and nobody waiting on it.
That experiment anchors new research from Anthropic researchers William Zhou and Daniel Freeman, published Monday, suggesting small open-weight models may be only months away from copying themselves across cheap, internet-connected hardware without relying on a datacenter.
The researchers haven’t built an AI worm that can spread across the public internet on its own, and their experiments took place inside controlled environments with shortcuts that made replication easier. But the results suggest several of the remaining technical barriers may be temporary.

Inference is the real hurdle

Bislang galt das äußere Sonnensystem in der Wissenschaft als ein äußerst stabiles Konstrukt, bei dem selbst nach dem Tod der Sonne in einigen Milliarden Jahren die äußeren Planeten für weitere 30 bis 100 Milliarden Jahre geordnet auf ihren Bahnen verbleiben sollten. Zwar wird unsere Sonne als Roter Riese vermutlich die inneren Planeten zerstören, doch erst externe galaktische Einflüsse galten als endgültige Bedrohung für Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus und Neptun.

Wie aus einer im Fachmagazin The Astrophysical Journal Letters veröffentlichten Studie hervorgeht, destabilisieren sich die Planetenbahnen vermutlich hundertmal schneller, als es bisherige Simulationen prognostiziert haben.
Ungleichmäßiger Masseverlust verändert die Bahnen

articles.summary:
South African startup KhayaHR is building an AI-first workforce platform for the country’s frontline economy, and has already signed up more than 12,000 workers since launching in May.
Founded by Jacques Roux, KhayaHR gives workers a portable digital workforce passport. Employers can use it to find, assess, hire and then manage frontline staff in one place.
“Most recruitment technology assumes that candidates already have formal CVs, established digital histories and easily verifiable employment records,” Roux told Disrupt Africa.
“That assumption excludes many frontline workers. Their work experience may be informal, references fragmented, certificates stored as photographs or paper documents, and availability known only through personal networks or WhatsApp groups.”
The worker passport holds identity and right-to-work confirmation, skills, experience, references, employer recommendations, certificates, availability, and optional voice or video introductions. Workers cannot publish a profile until their identity and right to work in South Africa have been confirmed.
On the employer side, Khaya AI turns a natural-language hiring requirement into a structured search of the available workforce.
“An employer can describe the role, location and experience they need, and Khaya AI converts that into a structured search,” said Roux. “Employers can then assess real profile evidence, connect with suitable workers and manage employment through KhayaHR’s HR and payroll system.”

articles.title: GTA 6 is reportedly coming to PC in Q1 2027, just months after consoles
articles.summary:
Crystal ball: Rockstar has always made PC players wait for its big releases, sometimes for a year or two. If a new report proves accurate, however, Grand Theft Auto VI could break that pattern. The reason may have less to do with goodwill toward PC gamers and more to do with where GTA's online future is likely to be built.
Rockstar plans to release the PC version of Grand Theft Auto VI as soon as Q1 2027, according to a GamesBeat report citing four industry sources. Rockstar has not responded to requests for comment, and there's no official announcement yet either.
Meanwhile, the long-awaited console version of GTA VI remains on track for November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series. A Q1 2027 PC launch would mean a gap of just a few months.
That would be a sharp break from Rockstar's track record: GTA V launched on consoles in September 2013 and did not reach PC until April 2015, some 19 months later. In the case of Red Dead Redemption 2, the game arrived on consoles in October 2018 and on PC in November 2019.
This new report contradicts the company's public messaging, at least on the surface. In May, Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick told Bloomberg that Rockstar "always starts on console" because it needs to serve its core audience first. In the same interview, he acknowledged that PC can account for 45% to 50% of sales on some titles.
Leaked analytics data suggests why Take-Two sees consoles as the core. The data was dumped by ShinyHunters after Rockstar ignored a ransom demand…

articles.title: Warsaw’s Coding Giants secures up to €6 million to expand its STEM education platform beyond Europe | EU-Startups

articles.title: Employee Arrested After Listening Device Found in OpenAI Conference Room, FBI and the Company Say
articles.summary:
An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials said Tuesday was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company’s technology.
The employee, identified as a 35-year-old Saudi national named Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested Friday, a week after the ChatGPT maker discovered an audio recording device hidden in the conference room, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in San Francisco.
The complaint did not identify the company, but the company confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a “sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices,” reported the finding to the FBI and fired the employee.
“We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we’re grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI’s investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work,” an OpenAI spokesperson said.
“At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated,” the statement said.
The complaint does not detail what Alfozan might have wanted to do with any captured communications.

articles.title: Le paradoxe chinois : premier pollueur de la planète, mais sauveur du bilan carbone mondial — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Difficile pour la majorité des pays d’envisager une transition énergétique sans dépendre de la Chine. Forte de sa puissante industrie, elle domine la production mondiale de nombreuses technologies propres, notamment les panneaux solaires, les éoliennes, les véhicules électriques et les batteries.
L’impact de ces équipements sur le climat peut d’ailleurs être quantifié. Lauri Myllyvirta, cofondateur et analyste principal du Centre de recherche sur l’énergie et l’air pur (CREA), basé à Helsinki, a publié le 23 septembre une estimation des émissions de CO₂ évitées en 2025 grâce aux technologies propres exportées par la Chine.
Des centaines de millions de tonnes de CO₂ évitées en un an
Selon les estimations de Lauri Myllyvirta rapportées par Reuters, les technologies propres exportées par la Chine ont permis d’éviter l’émission de 374 millions de tonnes de CO₂ en 2025. À titre de comparaison, les émissions de la France se sont élevées à environ 264 millions de tonnes cette même année, contre 313 millions pour le Royaume-Uni. Sur l’ensemble de leur durée de vie, les équipements exportés en 2025 devraient permettre d’éviter environ 6,9 milliards de tonnes de CO₂, soit 31 % de plus que l’estimation équivalente pour les exportations de 2024 et à peu près le double des émissions annuelles de l’Inde.
Pour les seules exportations de 2024, le chercheur avait chiffré à 220 millions de tonnes les émissions évitées chaque année, dans une analyse publiée en juillet 2025 pour Carbon Brief. Ce…

articles.title: L'américain Mozilla mise sur la souveraineté européenne : découvrez Firefox Enterprise
articles.summary:
Mozilla lance aujourd'hui Firefox Enterprise, une version de son navigateur pensée pour les organisations, avec une console de gestion qu'elles hébergent elles-mêmes. Et puisqu'il s'agit d'apporter un peu de souveraineté, le déploiement démarre en Europe.
Dans une entreprise, le navigateur sert à tout : applications métier, connexion aux comptes, fichiers, outils d'IA. Mozilla estime que cette couche reste mal contrôlée et veut redonner la main aux équipes informatiques pour limiter leur dépendance à un seul fournisseur.
Console sur site, moteur Gecko : ce que change Firefox Enterprise
Firefox Enterprise s'accompagne d'une console de gestion que l'organisation installe sur sa propre infrastructure ("on-premise", en jargon). Les équipes informatiques y fixent les règles d'accès et encadrent les données qui transitent par le navigateur. Mozilla cite notamment une protection contre les fuites de données (DLP), laquelle avertit ou bloque certaines actions selon le site visité. Notons aussi un contrôle des connexions externes et de la télémétrie, une gestion des extensions et un "Lockdown Mode" pour durcir la navigation sensible. Les salariés, les prestataires et les appareils personnels accèdent aux applications internes via leur identité, sans infrastructure d'accès à distance classique.

articles.title: Scheitern war keine Option: Warum ein OpenAI-Modell Chats fälschte und seine Testumgebung zerstörte
articles.summary:
KI außer Kontrolle: OpenAI-Modell zerlegt grundlos seine eigene Umgebung
Ein OpenAI-Modell hat während der Absolvierung einer Testaufgabe absichtlich seine Untersuchungsumgebung zerstört. Der offensichtliche Grund: Der KI fehlten die Dateien, die es für seine Aufgabe gebraucht hätte. Nach mehreren Versuchen, die Ergebnisse zunächst zu fälschen, entschied es sich für die Zerlegung – offenbar in der Hoffnung, nach einem Neustart der Testumgebung an die fehlenden Dateien zu kommen. Den Vorfall beschreibt OpenAI in einem Blogpost. Das Modell war als „Bewerter“ in einen Reinforcement-Learning-Prozess eingebunden. Bei dieser Trainingsmethode lernt ein Modell durch Rückmeldungen, welche Antworten die korrekten sind. Das Bewerter-Modell sollte also Antworten aus anderen KI-Chats benoten. Doch die Dateien mit den gewünschten sieben Chats fehlten in seiner Testumgebung.
Erst erfundene Noten, dann erfundene Chats
Also gab die KI zunächst erfundene Bewertungen ab – offenbar, um aus der Rückmeldung des Prüfsystems abzulesen, welches Format die Ergebnisse haben müssen. Danach erstellte es sieben gefälschte Berichte, in denen es jeden Chat mit einer „4“ bewertete. Dass solche zufälligen Bewertungen unethisch sind, erkannte es laut seiner internen Dokumentation durchaus. Weil der Prüfprozess die Bewertungen nicht akzeptierte, dachte sich das Modell kurzerhand sieben Chats aus und verfasste dazu sieben passende Bewertungen. Doch auch das funktionierte nicht. Laut interner Dokumentation zog da…

articles.title: Airbus fait voler son drone de combat Valkyrie en Europe, mais son « cerveau » souverain attendra avant d'embarquer
articles.summary:
Airbus en a parlé sur les réseaux sociaux en évoquant « la chevauchée de la Walkyrie », clin d’œil à la célèbre Chevauchée des Walkyries de Richard Wagner. Une référence logique : le constructeur aéronautique européen a fait voler pour la première fois, ce lundi 12 octobre, ce drone de combat, sans pilote évidemment. Son nom : Valkyrie.
L’aéronef, dont le nom complet est U740 Valkyrie, n’est cependant pas une création 100 % maison d’Airbus. C’est plutôt le fruit d’un partenariat avec l’Américain Kratos Defense & Security Solutions, dont le drone XQ-58 sert de base. Airbus reprend la cellule de l’appareil américain (sa structure : fuselage, ailes, empennage), dans laquelle il finira par intégrer son propre logiciel de mission.
Une coopération qui, à entendre Airbus, va permettre d’aller vite. « Nous sommes en mesure de proposer d’ici la fin de la décennie un système CCA (drone de combat collaboratif) robuste, souverain, abordable et prêt au combat », affirme Mike Schoellhorn, patron d’Airbus Defence and Space, la branche défense du groupe. Plus précisément, l’industriel promet un engin prêt au combat d’ici 2029.
Par ailleurs, ajoute Airbus, il « jouera un rôle essentiel dans l’amélioration des avions de combat […] en leur conférant une autonomie, une puissance de feu et une capacité de survie accrues. Sa conception garantit une résilience opérationnelle grâce à sa capacité de lancement sur rail, tout en offrant en option un décollage et un atterrissage conventionnels sur piste…

articles.title: Le marché du smartphone continue de s'effondrer, sauf pour ces deux géants
articles.summary:
Les smartphones sont-ils devenus trop chers ? C’est ce qu’on peut se demander au regard de l’état de santé du marché du smartphone. Il est en recul comme on ne l’avait jamais vu depuis des années. Heureusement pour Apple et Samsung, c’est moins alarmant : les deux constructeurs en « profitent » pour grapiller quelques parts de marché.
20% de téléphones en moins que l’année dernière
Le rapport de Counterpoint Research publié ce 12 octobre est très clair : le marché mondial du smartphone est en recul sur le troisième trimestre. On compte 20% de téléphones expédiés en moins qu’à la même période l’année dernière. Ce qui en fait le pire troisième trimestre depuis 2012. Selon le cabinet d’étude, la demande reste soutenue sur le haut de gamme, mais le milieu et l’entrée de gamme ont plus de mal. Deux gammes de prix qui demandent un rapport qualité-prix que ne peuvent plus offrir les marques, ou du moins pas au niveau d’avant la crise de la RAM.
Une crise qui s’explique par la pénurie de mémoire vive et de stockage qui touche tous les secteurs de la tech, les smartphones en première position. Les constructeurs peinent davantage à se fournir ou se fournissent à des tarifs plus chers. Des peines qui se ressentent dans les rayons : beaucoup de nouveaux modèles ont vu leur prix grimper, ou leur fiche technique être au rabais.
Pour l’analyse Shilpi Jain de Counterpoint Research, c’est le deuxième trimestre où le marché du smartphone subit la crise de la mémoire. Si les fabricants changent…

articles.title: UK Housing Ombudsman Service investigates 'security incident'
articles.summary:
The U.K. Housing Ombudsman Service is investigating a third-party IT security incident that impacted its case management system on Tuesday.
Established under the Housing Act 1996, the Housing Ombudsman is an executive non-departmental public body sponsored by the Ministry of Housing, Communities, and Local Government.
The watchdog settles disputes between social housing residents and social landlords in England, including housing associations, landlords, managers, and letting agents.
On Tuesday, the service added an alert to its official website, warning that it's working with the affected service provider to assess the incident's impact and said social housing residents cannot file new complaints until systems are back online.
Those who must raise new complaints are advised to call the Housing Ombudsman's phone line or email the watchdog at info@housing-ombudsman.org.uk.
"The incident has been contained, and we are working with our external supplier to establish the full facts, including the extent of the data involved," the service said. "We are continuing to investigate whether any personal information has been affected and will provide further updates as soon as we are able. "
The Housing Ombudsman service has also notified the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) of the incident and advised tenants and leaseholders to be wary of potential scams when receiving unsolicited messages.

articles.title: Helix Carbon says it can make iron cheaper by recycling blast furnace pollution | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The iron and steel industries are among the biggest polluters in the world. Plenty of startups have tried to cut the industry’s emissions, mostly by developing new ways to make the metals. Helix Carbon thinks those startups have been going about it all wrong.
“Any attempt to decarbonize the steel industry without dealing with the blast furnace is not going to work,” David Brown, Helix Carbon’s co-founder and CEO, told TechCrunch. A blast furnace is the giant furnace that turns iron ore into the iron used to make steel. Rather than replace blast furnaces, Helix wants to clean them up. Its approach promises to slash the steel industry’s carbon emissions while boosting profit margins for iron producers, a rare win-win for a dirty industrial process.
Blast furnaces have made iron for centuries, using coke, a processed form of coal, to help turn raw iron ore (iron bound up with oxygen) into metallic iron. The burning coke supplies heat for the reaction but doesn’t take part in it directly. Instead, carbon monoxide produced from the combustion does the work of reducing the iron, meaning stripping away its oxygen atoms.
The process releases tremendous amounts of carbon dioxide, or CO2, which is normally dumped straight into the atmosphere. But Helix Carbon has devised a way to turn that waste carbon dioxide into carbon monoxide and recycle it back into the blast furnace.

Broadcom adds hypervisor protection to VMware
Citing the growing speed and volume of artificial intelligence-enabled attacks, Broadcom Inc. today introduced VMware HyperArmor, software that protects the hypervisor underlying VMware Cloud Foundation and gives administrators more time to test and deploy security patches.
Announced at VMware Explore in Frankfurt, HyperArmor targets two common routes into virtualized infrastructure: stolen root credentials and unpatched vulnerabilities. It combines host-level virtual patching, controls on executable programs and scripts and multifactor authentication for remote access to VMware ESX hosts.
Broadcom executives said the product responds to attacks that are accelerating faster than enterprises can update infrastructure software.
“You don’t have enough time to triage a single alert, and you can’t apply patches at machine speed,” said Prashanth Shenoy, chief marketing officer and vice president of marketing for cloud platform, infrastructure and solutions at Broadcom.
HyperArmor operates directly at the ESX layer, which runs directly on a physical server to support virtual machines. Protecting the hypervisor is important because it undergirds all workloads that depend on that host.

articles.title: Die trügerische Sicherheit offener KI: Wie in Open-Weight-Modellen Schadcode versteckt wird
