Die Bereitstellung sogenannter Open-Weight-Modelle ist in der Softwareentwicklung etabliert. Im Gegensatz zu Closed-Source-Ansätzen gewähren die Herausgeber hierbei den Zugriff auf die fertig trainierten Parameter, die sogenannten Gewichte, des neuronalen Netzes.
Das vermittelt Anwender:innen den Eindruck, die Architektur nachvollziehen und auf Sicherheitsrisiken prüfen zu können. Ein Team von Wissenschaftlern um Andis Draguns vom Forschungsinstitut Contramont Research aus dem kalifornischen San Francisco und der britischen Universität Oxford belegt, dass diese Annahme fehlerhaft ist.
Kryptografische Schließfächer in Open-Weight-Modellen
Wie in einer auf dem Preprint-Server Arxiv veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, haben die Forscher eine Methode entwickelt, um Fähigkeiten in den Gewichten von KI-Modellen zu verstecken. Sie nutzen das Konzept der sogenannten Digital Lockers, bei dem Daten kryptografisch versiegelt werden.
Die Wissenschaftler verschlüsseln ein ausführbares Sub-Netzwerk und betten es in ein größeres Trägermodell ein. Dafür nutzen sie die Hash-Funktion Keccak, die unter anderem die Basis für den aktuellen Verschlüsselungsstandard SHA-3 bildet.

XMEMS starts mass-producing chips that cool AI glasses, smartphones and data centers
Silicon chip startup xMEMS Labs Inc. today said it has started mass production of its XMC-2400 and XMC-4800 chips for cooling artificial intelligence hardware.
No one has commercialized solid-state active cooling at this scale before, according to the company.
The chips are aimed at AI hardware running into heat limits in two places. Conventional fans “simply cannot fit” in AI glasses and smartphones that still need active heat removal, said Mike Housholder, vice president and general manager of the thermal management business unit at xMEMS. For data centers, the company is targeting solid-state drives, laser modules and other parts left outside the liquid cooling that increasingly surrounds high-power processors.
The technology behind both chips came out of the company’s speaker business, where an electrical signal flexes a thin silicon membrane to produce sound. In the cooling chips, the same type of membrane moves air. Device makers can route the air down narrow channels to a processor or a memory chip, the company said, since it builds high pressure.
Nothing in the package spins. Because each device is a single piece of silicon, Housholder said, it could eventually be packaged together with the AI processors it cools.
Personal SSDs and glasses built for AI or extended reality are the target for the XMC-2400. The XMC-4800 moves more air, enough for thermally demanding AI smartphones as wel…

Aunque hay quien prefiere conducir, como María Inmaculada Jiménez, quien lleva la gerencia de un restaurante en La Cala de Mijas (Málaga), pero vive en Mollina, en el interior de la provincia. Según contaba El Mundo, recorre 220 kilómetros diarios entre ida y vuelta para poder pagar una casa que en la costa no podría permitirse.
Es un caso extremo pero no aislado que en inglés denominan super-commuting. El problema es el de siempre: que la tecnología te permite vivir lejos del trabajo no significa nada en sí mismo. Porque la argolla sigue siendo la misma: salario insuficiente para pagar una casa.
A todos lados con portátil. Un estudio de Stanford sobre dos millones de trayectos en las diez mayores ciudades de EEUU detectó que los desplazamientos de 40 millas (unos 64 km) o más han pasado del 15,8% al 18,5% del total desde la pandemia. Los supercommutes de 75 millas (unos 120 km) o más han crecido casi un tercio hasta rondar el 3% de los trayectos, y suelen costar unas dos horas y veinte por sentido.
Quien no tiene que ir a la oficina cada día tolera un trayecto largo una o dos veces por semana si a cambio gana espacio y nivel de vida, claro. Pour protéger l’échange des clés, Surfshark utilisait déjà ML-KEM, un algorithme conçu pour empêcher le déchiffrement ultérieur du trafic intercepté aujourd’hui, même à l’aide d’un ordinateur quantique suffisamment puissant.

articles.title: Anthropic warns self-replicating AI could spread to your smart devices
articles.summary:
Anthropic is warning that small AI models could soon be able to self-replicate across consumer IoT devices, from Android TV boxes to smart ovens, creating distributed botnets capable of running AI workloads without relying on data centers.
The company's experiments showed that models could identify unfamiliar devices, connect them into a network, and prepare them to run an AI model.
Although the researchers successfully distributed the Gemma4-26B-A4B model from Google DeepMind on 15 off-brand Android TV boxes, they did not demonstrate a fully autonomous, self-replicating AI worm running on real IoT hardware.
However, they estimate that smaller models could achieve self-replication by the end of the year if they continue to improve at their historical rate.
“Our experiments suggest that small AI models may be months away from being capable enough to self-replicate on commercial internet-of-things (IoT) devices, like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes,” Anthropic warns.
“ A replicator like this would be challenging to shut down, since there’s no centralized point to shut off—though it may be slow (with a doubling time of days).”
Replication experiment
Anthropic ran its replication experiment using cheap Android TV boxes, and the AI models Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma4-26B-A4B, Llama3.1-8B, Opus 4.8, and GLM-5.2, each assigned a different role.

Singapore-based solid-state transformer (SST) startup Amperesand aims to help AI data centers smooth the spikes in their electrical demand that can stress power grids.
“When a glitch happens, we don’t just kick off the grid; we actually power the AI load with a battery,” Amperesand CEO Brian Dow told EE Times. “We also can pull power to keep the rate of change in the medium voltage under control.”
Dow noted a recent data center failure he hopes to help prevent: a July 2026 grid disconnection in the U.S. state of Virginia that caused data centers to automatically switch to backup generators, dropping a more-than 3-gigawatt load in seconds that caused power to flicker across the eastern U.S.
“A gigawatt is probably the power consumption of Cincinnati,” Dow said. “It’d be like Cincinnati turning all its lights on and off at every single load, simultaneously.”
SSTs are set to enter AI data centers as traditional transformers made of copper coils and magnetic iron cores struggle to meet rising demands for efficiency, power density, and scalability. Increasing rack power levels and fluctuating AI workloads cause energy losses, thermal challenges, and system complexity, power IC maker Microchip noted. SSTs directly convert medium-voltage grid power like 13.8 kV to 35 kV AC into high-voltage 800 VDC in a single step.

articles.title: VPN dark web alerts vs. free tools: Are you paying extra for repackaged data?

VPN dark web alerts vs. free tools: Are you paying extra for repackaged data?
VPN providers are increasingly selling “dark web alerts” as premium security features, marketing them as essential protection against identity theft. This raises a key question: do paid alerts find unique threats, or just repackage data that's freely available?
With subscriptions to the best VPNs already costing up to $10-15 monthly, adding identity protection features can push bills toward $20 a month. If you’re essentially paying for data available at no cost, that’s money better spent elsewhere.
This article is the third in a series of content relating to Cybersecurity Awareness Month 2026, which runs throughout October. The previous articles have covered VPN protection when using AI, and the benefits of dedicated antivirus over packaged solutions.
How dark web monitoring works
Let’s clear up a common misconception first: VPN services aren’t sending security analysts to actively patrol the dark web hunting for your name. That would be impossible – the dark web is too vast and constantly shifting.
Instead, what most dark web monitoring services actually do is simpler: they cross-reference your information against massive databases of leaked credentials that have already been publicly disclosed. These databases contain billions of compromised accounts from data breaches spanning over a decade.

Science Corporation CEO Max Hodak announced that the company has implanted its vision-restoring chip, PRIMA, into its first patient with Stargardt disease, an inherited eye disease that gradually destroys central vision. Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, the brain implant company, explained onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how the company’s work with PRIMA fits into its broader pursuit of a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).
“The retina is part of the central nervous system,” Hodak said. “We consider cochlear implants, retinal prostheses, motor prostheses, these are all different types of BCIs.”
Hodak outlined a vision in which BCIs expand into a wide range of medical technology applications, rather than simply being a way to control computers.
While PRIMA is commercially available in Europe for patients who’ve lost their sight to geographic atrophy, an advanced form of age-related macular degeneration, the company believes its approach can be applied to multiple diseases, including Stargardt disease, which is currently considered incurable.
Stargardt disease affects the outer retina, causing the gradual death of the eye’s light-sensing cells while potentially sparing the inner retina, the part that passes visual signals onto the brain. It causes a central blind spot that gradually enlarges over time. Approximately 150,000 people worldwide have lost vision due to the disease.

Cybersecurity company Trellix today launched Trellix Wise for Private Cloud to let enterprises run its artificial intelligence engine for security operations entirely inside their own environments.

articles.title: Ghostscript flaw lets hackers hijack servers via PDF uploads
articles.summary:
A critical heap buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-39919) in the Ghostscript interpreter and rendering engine could allow remote code execution through specially crafted PDF files.
The flaw was discovered on August 23 by researchers at Defiant's platform Wordfence using their Argus AI-powered system.
Ghostscript is a PostScript and PDF interpreter that can render PDFs as images, generate thumbnails for previews, and optimize PDF files by compressing embedded images and removing unnecessary font data.
When generating a PDF thumbnail, WordPress can use the PHP Imagick extension to call ImageMagick, which launches Ghostscript.
A specially crafted PDF file containing a JPEG 2000 image can trigger incorrect handling of low-bit-depth samples and mismatched component resolutions.
Using Argus, the researchers developed two exploits for CVE-2026-39919 that force Ghostscript to write 1,024 bytes into a 256-byte buffer, corrupting nearby memory and leading to unauthenticated remote code execution in a WordPress deployment.
Wordfence focused on WordPress systems, but notes that the flaw affects any online system running Ghostscript 9.21 through 10.07.1 and is exploitable if the payload is adjusted to the environment.
The researchers tested ten Linux environments, including Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, Alpine, and AlmaLinux, as well as an official WordPress Docker image snapshot, and found that all contained the vulnerable code.

articles.title: La seconde va être redéfinie d'ici 2030 : pourquoi les horloges atomiques au césium ne suffisent plus
articles.summary:
Tic, tac… Le bruit vient à l’esprit au moment de parler de ce qu’est une seconde. Car si pour le commun des mortels, cette unité n’est que la cadence d’une horloge, ou un soixantième de minute, la vision est toute autre du côté des scientifiques.
Du mardi 13 au jeudi 15 octobre, la Conférence générale des poids et mesures (CGPM) réunit au Palais des congrès de Versailles les délégués des 69 États membres du Bureau international des poids et mesures (BIPM). Au menu, entre autres, une résolution sur la future définition de la seconde, soumise au vote ce jeudi.
Ici, pas d’horlogers, mais des physiciens, car il faut remonter à la source de la définition de cette unité. La seconde atomique telle qu’on la connaît aujourd’hui a été définie le 13 octobre 1967, en France.
C’était à l’occasion de la 13e Conférence générale des poids et mesures, qui a fixé la seconde à la durée de 9 192 631 770 oscillations du rayonnement émis par un atome de césium 133 quand il change de niveau d’énergie. Le but n’est donc pas tant de diviser une journée en parts égales, mais plutôt de se baser sur les propriétés de la matière, bien plus stable.
La plus précise des mesures, mais toujours pas assez
La seconde est réalisée avec une incertitude relative de l’ordre de 10⁻¹⁶, ce qui en fait l’unité de base la plus précise du Système international, bien plus que le kilogramme ou l’ampère. Cela dit, même cette exactitude extrême ne suffit plus aujourd’hui en raison des progrès réalisés par les nouvelles génér…

A Saudi OpenAI engineer has been arrested for allegedly planting a hidden recording device in an executive conference room at the company's San Francisco offices to secretly record sensitive conversations.
The U.S. Department of Justice announced Tuesday that Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, who had worked at OpenAI since July 2025, was arrested on October 9 and charged with illegally intercepting oral communications.
The DOJ says OpenAI security personnel discovered the recording device on September 30, plugged into a USB port behind a television in an executive conference room.
According to the DOJ, OpenAI determined that the device had been concealed in toilet paper, was installed around September 28, and contained encrypted data.
"On or about Sept. 30, OpenAI personnel discovered a surreptitious audio recording device (Recording Device 1) inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room inside one of their buildings in San Francisco," says the DOJ press release.
The DOJ says the conference room was regularly used for meetings involving confidential information about OpenAI's proprietary research, product plans, technical capabilities, business relationships, and government engagements.
Security camera footage allegedly showed Alfozan near the conference room on multiple occasions, despite not being authorized to attend meetings held there.
According to the complaint, Alfozan also used a productivity tool to search for information about OpenAI's…

Quatre ans plus tard, Apple prend donc la peine de revoir son boîtier TV et la marque de Cupertino a un objectif précis : transformer ce simple cube dédié au streaming en véritable hub domotique.

2021 von den Ex-Googlern Noam Shazeer und Daniel De Freitas gegründet, ermöglicht es Character AI Nutzerinnen, mit verschiedenen echten oder fiktiven Persönlichkeiten wie Elon Musk, Albert Einstein oder Super Mario zu chatten. Zudem können Nutzer:innen sich eine eigene KI-Persönlichkeit programmieren, um sich mit ihr zu unterhalten.
Milliardenbewertung ganz ohne Einnahmen
2023 erreichte die KI-Plattform monatlich 100 Millionen Besuche, hatte aber bis dahin noch keinen einzigen Cent eingenommen. Trotz fehlenden Umsatzes sammelte Character.ai in einer von Andreessen Horowitz angeführten Finanzierungsrunde 150 Millionen Dollar ein. Damit erreichte das Startup eine Bewertung von gut einer Milliarde Dollar.
Jetzt muss Character.ai Insolvenz nach dem Chapter-11-Verfahren anmelden. Es drücken Verbindlichkeiten in Höhe von 50 bis 100 Millionen Dollar. Das ist aber noch nicht alles. Als Grund für das Scheitern gab das Unternehmen „erhebliche rechtliche, regulatorische und operative Gegenwinde“ im vergangenen Jahr an.
Character AI: Finanzielle und rechtliche Probleme

AMD Showcases Its Next-Gen EPYC "Verano" CPU, Up to 192 Cores and LPDDR5X Memory
AMD showed off its next-generation EPYC "Verano" server CPUs during CEO Dr. Lisa Su opening keynote at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The new CPU is the first EPYC processor to support LPDDR5X memory via SOCAMM2 modules. Now AMD is mirroring rival NVIDIA's Vera CPU that already uses SOCAMM2 modules. The "Verano" processor sits within the EPYC 9006 "LP" family and is built on the same TSMC 2 nm process as the already-launched EPYC "Venice". While AMD "Venice" is the first EPYC processor based on Zen 6 architecture, "Verano" is optimized for AI tasks in agentic AI racks. For this, AMD plans to pair them with its own Instinct MI500 GPUs via xGMI connectivity at up to 112 Gbps. It will run on the new SP8 platform rather than Venice's SP7. When we first heard about "Verano", AMD indicated that the upcoming CPUs will feature up to 72 cores on a single-socket platform. However, that has now been updated to up to 192 cores.
From the initial information available, this could mean either a single large chip or a dual 96-core configuration. More details came from System360Cheese on X, who reported that the chip shown featured eight Zen 6 CCDs alongside two large IO dies and four LPDDR5X memory controllers. Jessica Tawil volvió a dar sus primeros pasos en más de una década con la ayuda de un exoesqueleto portátil. (Tomado de Instagram)
Jessica Tawil dio sus primeros pasos en más de una década con un exoesqueleto portátil, luego de que un accidente automovilístico ocurrido en Nueva Jersey, Estados Unidos, en noviembre de 2014 le provocara una lesión medular y la dejara paralizada de la parte inferior del cuerpo.
El video superó las 200 millones de reproducciones en Instagram, donde la joven de 27 años reúne más de 800 mil seguidores. La publicación acumuló más de 8 millones de me gusta y 140.000 comentarios.
Tawil tenía 16 años cuando sufrió el accidente. Desde entonces usa una silla de ruedas a diario y fue diagnosticada como parapléjica T6, una condición que le impide mover las piernas y la parte inferior de su cuerpo.
Aunque considera que posiblemente no vuelva a caminar de forma natural, el dispositivo le permitió ponerse de pie y avanzar. Al incorporarse, reaccionó con incredulidad: “Oh, Dios mío... está bien, está bien, está bien”.
Cómo es la tecnología detrás del exoesqueleto

Anthropics KI-Agent Claude Code ist nicht nur bei Privatanwender:innen beliebt. Auch im Unternehmens- und Arbeitsumfeld wird der Coding-Helfer rege genutzt. Zu rege sogar, wenn es nach Microsoft und Meta geht. Beide haben laut einem Bericht von The Information damit begonnen, die Nutzung von Claude Code intern herunterzufahren. Entwickler:innen werden dazu angehalten, weniger mit Anthropics KI zu arbeiten.
Warum Meta und Microsoft Claude Code einschränken
Solche Schritte hatte Microsoft schon im Mai 2026 angestoßen und damals seinen Entwickler:innen mitgeteilt, dass zahlreiche Claude-Code-Lizenzen im Laufe der kommenden Monate gekündigt werden sollen. Laut internen Berichten sollen sich auch deshalb die Prognosen für die KI-Ausgaben ebenfalls drastisch reduziert haben. Anfang des Jahres hatte Microsoft noch geplant, eine Milliarde US-Dollar für Anthropics KI auszugeben. Jetzt ist es in etwa ein Drittel weniger.
Bei Meta soll sich ein ähnliches Bild abzeichnen. Mittlerweile arbeiten deutlich weniger Entwickler:innen mit Claude Code als es noch Anfang des Jahres der Fall war. articles.title: Governo autoriza bloqueio de celulares em presídios sem ordem judicial • Tecnoblog

Governo autoriza bloqueio de celulares em presídios sem ordem judicial
Decreto permite interromper sinais de comunicação em áreas delimitadas e restringir aparelhos pelo IMEI.
O Governo Federal publicou nesta terça-feira (13/10) um decreto que permite bloquear celulares em presídios sem uma ordem judicial. A medida prevê a cooperação entre União, estados, Distrito Federal e Anatel para acelerar o bloqueio de celulares e de outros meios de comunicação usados ilegalmente.
O programa, assinado pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), já está valendo e vai atuar em duas frentes: restringir aparelhos identificados individualmente e interromper sinais de radiocomunicação em perímetros de segurança ao redor das unidades prisionais. A segunda opção depende de equipamentos bloqueadores e deverá seguir as condições técnicas definidas pela Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações.
As administrações penitenciárias estaduais e distrital serão responsáveis por identificar os casos e encaminhar informações técnicas. Os pedidos serão enviados por uma plataforma digital do Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública, integrada ao Sistema Nacional de Informações Penais (Sisdepen).
Segundo o Art. 6º do decreto, quando um celular for identificado individualmente, a solicitação será encaminhada ao fluxo do Banco Nacional de Celulares com Restrição, com o código IMEI do aparelho. Nos casos que envolvam bloqueio de sinais em áreas delimitadas, as informações serão direcionadas à Anatel.

Cisco’s OCP message: The network is now AI’s critical path, and openness is the price of admission
For most of its history, Cisco Systems Inc. won by building vertically integrated network products and asking customers to buy all of it. The company did very well with that model. Security, meanwhile, was something Cisco sold as a separate product line rather than something that was inherent to its infrastructure. Patching a core switch meant scheduling a maintenance window, crossing your fingers and hoping nothing broke.
Under Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel, Cisco has moved away from that model and embraced openness. That’s why I found Cisco’s announcements at this week’s Open Compute Project Global Summit in San Jose more interesting for what they reveal about the company than for the products themselves.
As Mike Wheatley outlined in his SiliconANGLE post, Cisco rolled out a new pluggable optics form factor with Nvidia Corp., shipped its first Silicon One G300 systems, introduced the G302 top-of-rack chip and a new out-of-band management platform, and brought its Live Protect runtime security capability to SONiC. His post detailed the announcements, but it’s worth a deeper look at why these matter for artificial intelligence and what they say about a Cisco trying to be both open and secure, neither of which were strengths before Patel.

La NASA et le département de l’Énergie unissent leurs forces pour faire du nucléaire le moteur de l’exploration spatiale. L’enjeu est majeur, car les rivaux des États-Unis sont, eux aussi, à l’affût.
Le texte a été signé ce 8 octobre par Jared Isaacman, administrateur de la NASA, et le secrétaire à l’Énergie, Chris Wright. Il fixe un cadre commun pour la recherche, les essais, le lancement et l’exploitation des systèmes nucléaires, dans l’idée de confirmer la « supériorité spatiale » des États-Unis. De quoi permettre à l’agence spatiale d’avancer sur trois projets majeurs.
Trois projets majeurs déjà en cours
À commencer par le Space Reactor-1 Freedom, ou SR-1. Prévu pour la fin 2028, il s’agira du tout premier vaisseau interplanétaire propulsé par la fission nucléaire. À noter que son réacteur ne démarrera que 48 heures après le décollage, une fois l’engin sorti de l’attraction terrestre. Il alimentera ensuite des moteurs électriques qui le conduiront jusqu’à Mars.
Une fois sur place, il devrait larguer trois petits hélicoptères de la famille d’Ingenuity : c’est la mission Skyfall. Équipés de caméras et de radars capables de sonder le sol, ils repéreront de futurs sites d’atterrissage et chercheront de l’eau sous la surface. Et ce vol d’essai doit préparer la suite avec Lunar Reactor-1, un réacteur prévu pour 2030. Il devra alimenter la future base lunaire de la NASA pendant les périodes d’obscurité, quand le solaire ne suffira pas

Canada is continuing to improve its national EV infrastructure, adding nearly 100 new stations and 400 new charging ports in the third quarter of 2026.
Paren, a data intelligence company focused on North American electric vehicle (EV) charging infrastructure, released its “State of the EV Charging Industry” report for Q3 2026, which is focused on the current quarterly situation of Canada’s EV Charging infrastructure.

articles.title: “Lo que diga la sede central es irrelevante. Somos PlayStation”, confiesa exdirectivo cuando diseñaba la PS3, PS4 y PS Vita

“Cuando era presidente de Sony Computer Entertainment y gestionaba el negocio de consolas de sobremesa de PlayStation, cada vez que Howard Stringer y los demás ejecutivos me decían esto o aquello, yo me iba por mi propio camino diciendo: ‘Lo que diga la sede central es irrelevante. Somos PlayStation’”, relató Hirai en una entrevista con Nikkei XTrend.
La división de videojuegos funcionaba con un margen de independencia dentro de Sony que Hirai utilizaba para proteger las decisiones de PlayStation frente a la estructura corporativa. Esa lógica marcó su forma de conducir el área durante años de cambios para las consolas PS3, PS4 y PlayStation Vita.
Cómo fue la gestión de Kazuo Hirai en PlayStation
La desconfianza interna fue uno de los primeros obstáculos de su gestión. Hirai recordó que muchos trabajadores se preguntaban: “¿Cuándo nos va a quitar el suelo de bajo los pies?” o “¿Quizá es de los que se cuelgan el mérito y culpan a sus subordinados de los fallos?”.
El entonces director ejecutivo consideraba que la recuperación de la compañía requería reconstruir el vínculo con su personal. “Sin respeto, nadie va a pensar: ‘¡Vamos a trabajar duro juntos!’”, sostuvo.

articles.title: Spranic builds spatial memory for physical AI - SiliconANGLE

Spranic builds spatial memory for physical AI
Physical AI needs context about its surroundings to adapt beyond a fixed set of instructions.
Munich-based Spranic is building a spatial memory layer that records physical spaces and how they change. Connecting that information with knowledge graphs could help robots interpret their environments across different tasks, according to Jordi Spranger (pictured), founder and chief executive officer of Spranic.
“Robots deserve the right context at the right time across domains,” he said. “This is the problem we’re tackling. We can see that this works really well for digital agents already. Now we’re bringing this to the physical world.”
Spranger spoke with theCUBE Research’s John Furrier for theCUBE + NYSE Wired: AI Luminaries interview series on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how knowledge graphs could help robots adapt tasks and make their decisions auditable. (* Disclosure below.)
Giving physical AI reusable context
Adapting machines to changing environments remains a challenge for physical AI. Reusable spatial context can reduce the task-specific planning required for robot deployments, according to Spranger.
“But for robots, maps are a really big part,” he said. [Robots] need Google Maps on steroids to be really free from a statically planned task [so they] can replan across a lot of tasks that a humanoid could do.”

articles.title: Los reactores SMR llevan años prometiendo una revolución nuclear que todavía no termina de arrancar
articles.summary:
Más rápidos de construir, más económicos, más seguros… Los reactores modulares pequeños (SMR, por sus siglas en inglés) parecían, hace no tanto, haber llegado para resolver los principales retos de la energía nuclear convencional. Pero el tiempo ha pasado y no solo esos SMR no han terminado de cuajar, sino que, además, la energía nuclear ha estado en pleno retroceso.
Por lo menos hasta ahora, porque es verdad que algo está cambiando. La construcción nuclear vuelve a la agenda pública, como muestra, por ejemplo, el caso del gobierno de Georgia Meloni en Italia, que ha roto con la inercia europea de cerrar plantas nucleares. Sin embargo, incluso en este “renacer nuclear” que puede que se dé, parece que los SMR no terminan de despegar o no al ritmo que nos habían prometido. ¿Por qué?
¿Qué es exactamente un SMR? Según la Agencia Internacional de la Energía Atómica (IAEA), los reactores modulares pequeños son reactores nucleares con una capacidad de hasta 300 MW por unidad; es decir, un tercio de lo que genera un reactor convencional. Una de las principales ventajas que presentan es que, precisamente por su tamaño, son mucho más fáciles de transportar y ensamblar en plantas que, ya de por sí, pueden ser mucho más pequeñas que las centrales habituales.
Además, según este organismo, estos reactores pueden ser más seguros, ya que su diseño, mucho más sencillo, se basa a menudo en sistemas pasivos y en las propias características del módulo, como la baja potencia. Esto da un mayor mar…

articles.title: Llevamos años cambiando las sábanas cada semana. La ciencia apunta a que lo importante no es cuándo las cambias, sino cómo las lavas
articles.summary:
Dentro de los hogares hay diferentes debates en torno a con qué frecuencia hacer diferentes tareas, como por ejemplo el cambio de sábanas de nuestras camas. Aquí hay familias donde las sábanas se cambian cada semana, en otras cada dos y otras personas que se olvidan completamente de esto. Pero aquí los expertos apuntan a que lo importante está sobre todo en la temperatura de lavado.
El origen de los siete días. Aunque es un consejo que se ha transmitido entre las diferentes generaciones de una familia, la realidad es que la cifra de los 7 a 10 días no sale de ningún ensayo clínico. Aquí debemos entender que este rango de fechas responde a una pauta de control específica para las personas alérgicas a los ácaros del polvo. Y está avalado por las instituciones sanitarias.
Además, tenemos como referencia un estudio clásico de Vyszenski-Moher publicado en 2002 que demostró que las especies comunes de ácaros no necesitan un cambio de sábanas cada semana, sino que hace falta una temperatura alta para romper su ciclo vital. Es por ello que estamos ante un mito temporal, puesto que no existe ningún estudio primario que demuestre que cambiar las sábanas cada 7 días frente a cada 14 tenga un impacto real en la salud de la población general.
La verdadera clave. Aunque estamos obsesionados con seguir una rutina concreta, la clave está en la temperatura del agua con la que lavamos las sábanas. Y aquí un estudio publicado en 2008 nos descubrió lo que pasaba con los ácaros a diferentes tempe…

WhatsApp cuenta con una función para revisar los dispositivos que mantienen acceso a una cuenta, una verificación que permite detectar sesiones abiertas en computadoras, tabletas u otros aparatos.
La función se llama “Dispositivos vinculados” y muestra los aparatos asociados a la aplicación de Meta, incluidos aquellos que podrían haber quedado conectados sin que el titular de la cuenta lo advierta.
La revisión es útil para quienes utilizan WhatsApp Web en una computadora compartida, en una oficina, un cibercafé o un aparato prestado. Encontrar un acceso desconocido no confirma por sí solo que alguien haya espiado los chats, pero sí exige cerrar la sesión y reforzar la seguridad de la cuenta para evitar accesos sin autorización.
Dónde se revisan los dispositivos vinculados a la cuenta de WhatsApp
El listado está disponible desde la app instalada en el teléfono. Mais cedo, o governo também publicou medidas para facilitar a fiscalização de celulares em presídios.
As empresas poderão continuar usando chatbots, assistentes virtuais e sistemas de inteligência artificial para fazer triagens, encaminhar solicitações e resolver demandas. Porém, precisarão garantir uma opção de atendimento por uma pessoa:

Incluso con el nuevo esquema, Google aseguró que Argon seguirá siendo más barato que sus rivales directos por cada token procesado. La compañía también afirmó que el modelo superó a GPT-6 Astra, a Claude Fable 5.1 y a Claude Opus 5.5 en pruebas comparativas de programación, ciberseguridad, ciencia, finanzas y derecho.
Esas comparaciones surgieron de pruebas que la propia Google diseñó y ejecutó, una práctica habitual entre las empresas de inteligencia artificial que todavía no cuenta con una verificación independiente generalizada.
El modelo también amplió a un millón de tokens el límite de texto que puede generar en una sola tarea, 16 veces más que el tope anterior de 64.000 tokens que tenía Gemini 3.

articles.summary:
AI model ‘self-replication’ is only months away, Anthropic says — and it doesn’t even need a data center to happen
Smaller models are already capable of hijacking unfamiliar hardware
- Anthropic warns that self-replicating AI worms could become feasible by the end of the year
- These AI worms could hijack hardware ranging from IoT devices to data centers
- Smaller models are already capable of adapting to unfamiliar hardware and self-replication
Anthropic has warned self-replication could become feasible for small AI models on internet-of-things (IoT) devices in just a matter of months.
This could be a big problem because a self-replicating AI model does not have a centralized off-switch and could hop networks to discover other IoT hardware to further replicate without human control.
Anthropic warns these AI worms could use multiple compromised IoT devices to run inference while carrying its model weights with it as it reproduces. IoT devices would be a prime target for this worm because they are “cheap and typically poorly defended,” the company says.
Small AI models could spread quickly
To test the viability of a self-replicating AI worm, Anthropic researchers ran Gemma4-26B-A4B - a 25 billion parameter model - across 15 inexpensive off-brand Android TV boxes at a cost of around $55 each. Once networked together the TV boxes were able to run distributed inference, solidifying the proof-of-concept.

Outre leurs nuisances sonores, les centres de données dégagent énormément de chaleur. Et pour les refroidir, les opérateurs font évaporer de l’eau, ce qui équivaut à une consommation directe. Mais ils requièrent aussi beaucoup d’électricité ; or, la produire nécessite également de l’eau, rappelle Bloomberg.

En plena Alpujarra granadina, Murtas es un pueblo de unos 400 habitantes con un solo bar. Y como adelantó ‘Ideal’, de sus 1.399 electores solo 332 residen allí. Los otros 1.067 figuran como residentes en el extranjero, según el INE, el 76% del censo. Su alcalde, José Miguel Romera, cuenta que la mayoría “no son gente del pueblo ni lo conocen”: sus familias emigraron en su día a Argentina o Venezuela.
La explicación de este fenómeno parte de la ‘ley de nietos’. Pero desde el lunes también es un problema judicial. El Tribunal Supremo mantiene el veto al voto de los nacionalizados por esa vía, y Murtas es uno de los ejemplos que se pusieron sobre la mesa. En la vista ante el Supremo, Iustitia Europa citó el municipio, con 330 vecinos y 1.038 inscritos en el CERA, el censo de españoles residentes en el extranjero.
¿Qué es la ‘ley de nietos’? Empecemos por el principio. Porque esta ley no existe como ley: es el apodo de la disposición octava de la Ley 20/2022 de Memoria Democrática, que dio la nacionalidad a hijos y nietos de españoles exiliados que la perdieron o renunciaron a ella. El plazo cerró el 22 de octubre de 2025. El Gobierno esperaba cerca de un millón de beneficiarios. Intel bets the next phase of AI belongs to the rightsized system, not the biggest one
For three years, artificial intelligence infrastructure has been dominated by one idea: Bigger is better. Bigger models, bigger clusters, and bigger checks written to a small group of suppliers. At this week’s Open Compute Project Global Summit, Intel Corp. argued that the next phase of AI will look very different and that Intel is well-positioned to benefit.
During his keynote, Nicolas Dubé (pictured), corporate vice president at Intel, framed his OCP keynote around a simple phrase: “Put every prompt in its place.” He shared new details about the Intel GPU D-series, formerly code-named Crescent Island, as well as Xeon rack designs built largely on OCP’s Open Rack v3 spec and open software work.
Underneath is a strategic argument worth attention: Intel believes inference, not training, will define enterprise AI economics and that agentic AI will bring the CPU back to the center of the data center. If that’s right, Intel’s turnaround gets a second engine at exactly the right time.
Not every prompt needs a frontier model
Today, most organizations default to sending every request to a frontier model, whether or not the task warrants it. That’s like hiring a senior law partner to proofread a memo. Intel’s alternative is an orchestration layer that evaluates each request based on the required depth of intelligence, context length, latency, data sensitivity and sovereignty, and cost and energy.

Le bitume sous nos semelles n'a rien d'immuable. Publiée le 12 octobre 2026 dans la revue Nature Cities, une étude pilotée par Shengli Tao et Xie Hu, chercheurs à l'université de Pékin, a mesuré entre 2014 et 2023 les mouvements verticaux du sol dans 465 villes de plus d'un million d'habitants, réparties sur 107 pays. Le phénomène porte un nom, la subsidence : un tassement lent qui lézarde les façades, tord les canalisations et aggrave les inondations. Les auteurs revendiquent la première évaluation planétaire menée avec une méthode homogène, là où les travaux antérieurs juxtaposaient des études locales aux protocoles disparates.

Mexico affiche une médiane plus modeste, 8 mm, mais certains de ses quartiers plongent d'environ 217 mm chaque année. Plus de 21 cm. Qué fue Roja Directa y por qué perdió vigencia
El sitio ganó notoriedad al reunir enlaces a transmisiones en vivo de partidos y eventos deportivos. Esa función generó una fuerte disputa con las empresas propietarias de los derechos de emisión, que vieron en la plataforma una amenaza directa a su modelo de negocio.
La oposición de ligas, productoras y operadores de televisión se tradujo en acciones judiciales y bloqueos constantes contra los distintos dominios asociados a Roja Directa. Con el paso del tiempo, la presión judicial fue en aumento.
Los accesos al sitio comenzaron a bloquearse desde distintos países y proveedores de internet, lo que generó una marcada inestabilidad en su funcionamiento.
Esa inestabilidad abrió la puerta a la aparición de numerosos clones: portales que imitan el nombre original pero no guardan relación alguna con sus creadores y que solo buscan captar visitas aprovechando la popularidad de la marca.

articles.summary:
Après quatre ans d’attente, Apple vient enfin de présenter une nouvelle génération de son Apple TV 4K. Plus puissant et désormais équipé pour Siri AI, le petit boîtier noir veut aussi devenir un élément central de la maison connectée.
Il était temps. Depuis 2022, Apple n’avait pas touché à son boîtier multimédia, pourtant régulièrement cité parmi les meilleurs appareils pour profiter de ses films et séries sur grand écran. Le constructeur profite de son événement « Welcome Home », organisé ce mardi 13 octobre, pour lui offrir une quatrième génération. Au programme, un nouveau processeur, une connectivité revue et surtout une intégration bien plus poussée de Siri. Les rumeurs de ces derniers jours avaient vu juste sur plusieurs points, mais Apple a aussi réservé quelques précisions importantes, notamment concernant la télécommande. De quoi donner un peu de relief à une gamme qui commençait sérieusement à prendre la poussière.
Siri AI s’invite dans le salon, sans avoir besoin de la télécommande
La principale nouveauté concerne l’arrivée de microphones directement intégrés à l’Apple TV 4K. Comme le confirme Apple dans son annonce officielle, il devient possible d’interroger Siri à distance, sans maintenir le bouton de la télécommande ou posséder un HomePod.
Une évolution bienvenue pour un appareil qui occupe déjà une place importante dans l’écosystème domestique du constructeur. Il suffit désormais de s’adresser au boîtier pour rechercher un programme ou contrôler ses accessoire…

articles.title: Robots could get a ‘ChatGPT moment’ in the next one to two years, Unitree chief says — and it’ll be powered by OpenAI’s GPT-7
articles.summary:
Unitree CEO says robotics breakthrough could happen in 2027 — with the 'ChatGPT moment' for embodied intelligence being powered by OpenAI's GPT-7 model
A new fast lane for humanoid robots?
- Unitree’s CEO says robotic AI could soon see a huge breakthrough
- Such a change could happen ‘next year,’ the CEO believes
- That could happen thanks to OpenAI’s upcoming GPT-7 model
AI is revolutionizing the world of software on a daily basis — you only need to look at how far vibe coding has come to see proof of that. But big changes could also be coming to robotics, with one company leader predicting that we could be on the cusp of seeing a “ChatGPT moment” in the industry.
That idea was put forward by Wang Xingxing, CEO of Chinese robotics firm Unitree. Speaking at an industry event in Shanghai, China (via the South China Morning Post), Wang declared that OpenAI’s recently released GPT-6 Astra model is so powerful that it has encouraged a belief that a breakthrough could occur “within one or two years.”
“It’s possible that, say, a GPT-7 model released next year could directly crack the problems of embodied intelligence” Wang said, referring to the idea of commanding a robotic device using artificial intelligence. That’s an advancement on Wang’s belief in August this year, when the CEO said that such a “ChatGPT moment” of technical ability could take a decade to arrive.

articles.title: Bumble no pudo ofrecer más amor: acordó venderse por USD 1.300 millones tras años de caída de usuarios
articles.summary:
Bumble será adquirida por Ithaca Holdings en una transacción totalmente en efectivo que valora a la empresa de aplicaciones de citas en USD 1.300 millones. Cuando la operación se complete, sus acciones dejarán de cotizar públicamente y la compañía pasará a operar como una empresa privada bajo el control de Ithaca.
Los accionistas de Bumble recibirán USD 6,05 por cada acción de Clase A. El precio representa una prima de aproximadamente 138% frente al valor de cierre de la acción el 9 de octubre de 2026: en otras palabras, Ithaca ofreció pagar 138% más que el precio que tenían los títulos antes de que se conociera la posible venta.
La oferta también equivale a una prima cercana al 119% respecto del precio promedio ponderado por volumen de las acciones durante los 30 días previos al 9 de octubre de 2026. El acuerdo fue anunciado el 13 de octubre de 2026.
Qué pasará con Bumble tras la compra
Una vez que se cierre la transacción, Bumble dejará de ser una empresa cotizante y sus acciones no podrán negociarse de forma pública. La compañía mantendrá sus oficinas en Londres, Austin y Nueva York, y se espera que conserve su sede en Austin, Texas.
Los codirectores ejecutivos de Ithaca Holdings, Ravi Gupta y John Hegeman, asumirán esos mismos cargos en Bumble.
La fundadora y directora ejecutiva de la empresa, Whitney Wolfe Herd, seguirá involucrada activamente en la compañía y trabajará con los nuevos directivos.

articles.summary:
'Somebody’s gotta pay for all the useless Siri AI no one likes': I love my Apple TV 4K, but there's nothing compelling about the more-expensive new model — and Apple fans online feel even more strongly about it
It's taken four years to do little more than double the price. I'm sitting this one out
I love my Apple TV 4K, which I think is the best streaming device you can buy if, like me, you're already all-in on Apple. But while my Apple TV 4K (2022) is great, it's also four years old. That's an eternity in TV tech, so I was excited to see what new features and capabilities the new Apple TV 4K announced today would bring.
Unfortunately, there are hardly any new features or capabilities. But the new Apple TV is much more expensive, so… uh, thanks?
What I saw today was a bit like if Apple took four years to make a new season of Pluribus, restricted it to a new Apple TV tier costing twice as much, and it turned out to be identical to Season 1 but 3% brighter and 5% faster.
I'm not the only Apple TV fan to be disappointed. Reddit is unhappy too.

articles.title: HomePod mini 2 : six ans après, Apple voit plus grand pour sa petite enceinte
articles.summary:
Six ans après le premier modèle, Apple dévoile enfin son HomePod mini de deuxième génération. Une enceinte plus puissante, avec quelques nouveautés bienvenues, mais dont la principale attraction ne sera pas disponible immédiatement.
Le HomePod mini aura pris son temps pour évoluer. Depuis son lancement en 2020, la petite enceinte connectée d’Apple n’avait connu que quelques changements de couleurs, malgré les progrès réalisés par Amazon et Google dans les assistants vocaux. Le constructeur profite de son événement « Welcome Home » pour lui offrir une véritable mise à jour matérielle, avec un processeur plus récent et de nouvelles possibilités audio. Siri AI occupe évidemment le devant de la scène, mais Apple a aussi réservé quelques surprises pour les amateurs de musique et de home cinéma. Reste à savoir si elles suffiront à convaincre les possesseurs du premier modèle de passer à la caisse.
Une nouvelle puce et un Siri AI qui se fait attendre
Le HomePod mini 2 conserve le design sphérique de son prédécesseur, mais abandonne la puce S5 au profit d’un processeur Apple S10, apparu avec l’Apple Watch Series 10. articles.title: MENA startup funding jumps to $1.65 billion in Q3, with Saudi Arabia taking the lead
articles.summary: Startup investment across the Middle East and North Africa more than doubled in the third quarter of 2026, driven by a wave of large Saudi fintech deals that helped revive funding activity despite persistent geopolitical uncertainty. Yet the recovery remained heavily concentrated in a handful of companies and markets, raising questions about whether the momentum can extend across the wider ecosystem. Startups across MENA raised $1.65 billion through 145 deals between July and September, up 108% from the previous quarter , while deal volume increased 39%. Despite the sharp quarterly rebound, funding remained approximately 63% below the $4.5 billion recorded during the same period last year . The recovery gained momentum in September , when regional funding exceeded $1.1 billion, following a subdued July and an August rebound driven largely by two UAE-based companies. Saudi Arabia reclaimed the lead from the UAE, accounting for the majority of capital deployed during the quarter. The composition of funding also showed a notable shift. Debt financing accounted for $441 million across 10 transactions, representing 26.8% of total investment, compared with almost 59% during 2025. Non-debt funding reached $1.21 billion, suggesting that the recovery was not solely dependent on credit-backed transactions. articles.title: Microsoft change la façon de créer les applications sur Windows 11
articles.summary:
Enfin, Microsoft permet plus de liberté aux développeurs avec WinUI Gallery 3.0 ! Cette nouveauté tant attendue va faciliter la création d'applications pour Windows 11.
Microsoft a modifié le fonctionnement de son application de démonstration destinée à la conception de logiciels sous Windows 11. La mise à jour vers WinUI Gallery 3.0 intègre désormais des composants expérimentaux issus du Windows App SDK, ce qui permet aux développeurs de tester de nouvelles commandes plus tôt dans leur cycle de développement, de manière à faciliter la création de certaines apps.
Un ajout des éléments d'interface anticipé
Jusqu'alors, les éléments d'interface n'étaient ajoutés à WinUI Gallery qu'après la sortie d'une version stable du Windows App SDK. Cette organisation limitait la capacité de Microsoft à ajuster ces commandes en fonction des retours des utilisateurs. Avec l'arrivée du SDK expérimental dans la version 3.0, les créateurs d'applications peuvent tester les fonctionnalités en amont et transmettre leurs remarques à temps pour orienter les modifications.
Cette version comprend ainsi de nouveaux exemples de commandes expérimentales, comme TableView, Charts, Wrap Panel et LayoutPanel, élaborés pour présenter les données de manière plus lisible.
Niels Laute, chef de produit senior chez Microsoft, a également détaillé plusieurs ajustements pratiques apportés à l'application :

articles.title: Low-Cost Android Phones Ship With Preinstalled Malware That Turns Them Into Residential Proxies
articles.summary:
Low-cost Android smartphones have been shipped with malicious software baked into the device firmware, allowing bad actors to covertly install apps, conduct ad fraud, and turn devices into residential proxies.
The activity, which targets Android devices built on MediaTek platforms across several brands, is being tracked by Bitdefender under the moniker Midnight Mimosa.
The preinstalled malware ("com.android.system.lite") runs with system-level privileges, which make it possible to install or uninstall a rotating set of at least 32 disguised apps, grant itself additional permissions to accessibility services, notifications, and SMS, and load arbitrary code supplied remotely by the operators.
Specifically, it fetches a remote configuration from an external server and then downloads and executes additional payloads designed to conduct ad fraud and silent installation or removal of partner apps. These apps incorporate proxyware, ad fraud, and code execution features. It can also grant permission to any Android app package.
"This essentially means its operators could install and delete apps at will, tuning each device to their needs, including making them part of large botnets," the Romanian cybersecurity company said.
"This scheme is likely designed mainly to generate revenue. The operators carry out ad and click fraud, collect device and installed-app information, and turn infected devices into residential-proxy relay nodes, making them zombies in botnets."

articles.title: GTA 6 Reportedly Coming to PC in Q1 2027
articles.summary:
Tuesday, October 13th 2026
GTA 6 Reportedly Coming to PC in Q1 2027
Rockstar is planning to bring GTA 6 to PC sometime in the first quarter of 2027, according to a new report from GamesBeat. The outlet cites four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans, all of whom asked to stay anonymous. If accurate, PC players would get the game between January and March 2027, just a few months after its November 19 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar still hasn't announced a PC version, and PC was left out of the launch plans from the start. Interestingly, if the timing pans out, that would be a much shorter wait than last time. GTA 5 hit consoles in September 2013 and only reached PC in April 2015, roughly 19 months later. 
This could matter for the roleplay ecosystem too, since FiveM, the framework behind most GTA 5 roleplay servers, runs only on PC, and GTA 6's online mode is already tipped for 2027. Of course, early PC launch windows have surfaced before that haven't exactly panned out. A Corsair executive floated an early 2026 launch last year, a comment Corsair later called speculation, and VGC's Andy Robinson suggested last month that the PC version might show up sooner than people expect. A Q1 2027 release would also arrive before Take-Two's fiscal year closes on March 31, 2027. Until Rockstar says something, readers are advised to treat this as a well-sourced rumor and not a confirmed date.

articles.title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
articles.summary:
Attackers took remote control of fridges and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets on the night of October 11 and warmed them, forcing stores to throw food away, several retail chains said.
The attackers reached them through the controller that runs all of a store's fridges and freezers, a device made by Danish company Danfoss that maintenance firms can manage remotely. Les Mousquetaires, which owns the Intermarché chain, said its fridges and freezers were put into defrost and heated to as much as 50°C.
CERT-FR, the French government's computer emergency response team, said in an alert published in French on October 12 that it is aware of numerous compromises affecting two Danfoss controller series, the AK-SM and the AK-SC. It told operators to disconnect the controllers or filter access to them.
CERT-FR is part of ANSSI, France's national cybersecurity agency. ANSSI's head, Vincent Strubel, called it urgent to take the two series off the internet or filter access very tightly, AFP reported.
Neither French authorities nor Danfoss has so far said who carried out the attack or how the attackers got into the controllers. Danfoss said most of the units hit were older models that it no longer updates.
Which Chains Were Hit

articles.title: LG Smart TVs Vulnerable to Pre-Auth Root Takeover From Local Network
articles.summary:
Three vulnerabilities in LG's webOS can be chained to give an attacker on the same local network root access to certain smart TVs without a PIN or any interaction from the owner.
LG has issued a fix, according to an advisory published by SSD Secure Disclosure on October 12.
The chain was tested on two TV models, the 32LQ636BPSA and the 27TQ600SW, running webOS 7.5.7-25 on firmware 04.54.40. Whether other models or firmware versions are affected is not known.
Owners of affected TVs should check for a firmware update. No workaround is available for those who cannot update yet.
The attack enters through a service that the TV exposes on port 3001, which is used by the LG ThinQ app for pairing. An attacker replays a manifest from sync-demo, a built-in app already on the device, signed with a test certificate the firmware trusts. A permission in the manifest causes the pairing service to skip the PIN prompt and hand over a privileged key.
With that key, the attacker launches another built-in app, cmp-client, and points it to an attacker-controlled page. The app does not check where it navigates, and the loaded page keeps access to PalmServiceBridge, an internal interface to the TV's system services.
Through that bridge, the attacker calls the system logging service, pmlogd, passing shell commands through an input field the service does not check. Because pmlogd runs as root, the injected command runs as root.

The dangerous part of a stolen identity isn't always the initial login. It's what an attacker can do with that access next.
With AI accelerating reconnaissance, exploitation of vulnerabilities, and privilege escalation, attackers can move through systems faster than security teams can investigate. A compromised account that looks legitimate at first could become the starting point for a much larger attack.
And that's where traditional identity security faces a serious problem: Checking who gets access isn't enough if you can't control what happens after.
Why Traditional Identity Controls Are Falling Behind
Many identity security controls focus on authentication, permissions, and access policies. But what happens when a trusted identity is compromised, its behavior changes, or an attacker begins exploiting already granted privileges?
That gap becomes more dangerous as AI-powered attacks accelerate.
Attackers can automate parts of the attack chain while defenders are still collecting alerts, investigating activity, and deciding how to respond.
The answer isn't simply detecting attacks faster. It's the ability to evaluate and control access in real time while an identity is actively being used.
This is the idea behind runtime identity security.

articles.title: SAP Discloses Critical CVSS 10 Flaw in Cloud SDK for Python Allowing OAuth2 Credential Theft
articles.summary:
A flaw in SAP's Cloud SDK for Python can send an application's OAuth2 client credentials to a server an attacker controls, SAP said in a security advisory on October 13. The flaw affects multi-tenant applications on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) that use the SDK, SAP's official Python client for BTP services. An attacker must be able to control the tenant subdomain, the name such an application passes to the SDK to say which tenant a request is for.
The flaw is tracked as CVE-2026-89111 and carries SAP's CVSS score of 10.0 out of 10. The advisory names version 0.45.2, released on August 21, as the fix.
The SDK handles authentication for those services with the application's client credentials, a client ID and a client secret. Version 0.45.2 added a check that rejects any tenant subdomain that is not a simple name.
Six later releases do not apply that check in every case, The Hacker News found. Versions 0.53.0 through 0.55.0, published between September 10 and September 18, skip it when an application calls the SDK's Destination service module.
Version 0.53.0 moved that module onto new shared code for requesting tokens, and that code did not include the check. Version 0.55.1 added it there on September 18.
Passing a tenant subdomain that contains URL delimiters "now raises ValueError immediately instead of silently routing credentials to an attacker-controlled endpoint," the 0.55.1 release notes say.

An attacker chained three zero-day flaws in Ivanti Connect Secure, a VPN appliance, to run commands as root without logging in, security firm Volexity said on October 13. Ivanti has released fixes for two of the flaws and told customers on affected versions to "act immediately." A fix for the third is still pending, according to Volexity.
Volexity, which reported the flaws to Ivanti, found the attack on one customer's appliance. The appliance was fully patched at the time and running version 22.8R2.4. The attacker, which Volexity tracks as UTA0576, began exploiting it on October 3.
Ivanti said on October 13 that it is aware of "limited exploitation in the wild."
The first two flaws are an authentication bypass and a remote code execution flaw, tracked together as CVE-2026-104935. Together they let an attacker run code as the appliance's cgi-server user, and the third flaw, a privilege escalation, raises that to root, Volexity said.
The CVE record Ivanti filed shows which Connect Secure versions are affected:

articles.title: Docker Fixes Critical Two-Year-Old Hub Flaw That Let One User Push Images as Another
articles.summary:
A flaw in Docker Hub, the registry where container images are published and downloaded, let one user push, pull, or delete images as another user. Docker fixed the flaw on September 30 and says it found no evidence that anyone exploited it.
The flaw was in the feature that converts a personal account into an organization, Docker said in a security advisory on October 12. Conversion transferred the account's personal access tokens (PATs) to the user designated as the organization's owner. A PAT is used in place of a password in the registry, and the person who created each token can still use it.
The access was limited to the registry. It did not reach the Docker Hub web interface, and it could not be used to change a password, email address, or two-factor settings, or to take over an account.
Docker tracks the flaw as CVE-2026-105445 and rated it critical. The CVE record it published on October 13 gives the flaw a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.4.
The flaw was open from August 26, 2024, until the fix, a little over two years. Docker made the fix on Docker Hub itself, so there is no update to install.
Docker Hub cannot move a repository from one account to another. A user instead converts a personal account into an organization that keeps the same name, and must name an existing account as its owner.

articles.title: Anthropic Warns Small AI Models Could Soon Form Self-Propagating IoT Botnets
articles.summary:
Small artificial intelligence (AI) models may be months away from developing capabilities to self-replicate on IoT devices like smart ovens and off-brand Android TV boxes, according to a warning from Anthropic.
The frontier AI lab said small AI models could form autonomous, self-propagating worm botnets that are "challenging to shut down," since "there's no centralized point to shut off."
Prior work has demonstrated that AI agents can act like one by scanning their network, executing an exploit, and copying model weights to a target machine across a GPU cluster with an aim to generate tailored attack strategies and use compromised machines as a botnet to run large language models (LLMs) in order to sustain its reasoning and expand in scale.
"Such an 'AI worm' could carry its model weights with it as it reproduces (or re-download them from a public hub), and then run inference directly on compromised hardware," Anthropic said. "Effectively, the weights would become part of the malware payload."
The idea, at a high level, explains how AI models could potentially break into internet-connected devices and use their computing power to run themselves and spread to other devices, without having to rely on expensive data centers all the time. A more powerful model that's too large to fit into a single device could be split into small chunks and run across multiple machines to collectively run it.

"Hundreds of CVEs in a single release used to be the exception; now it's the baseline," Dustin Childs, head of Threat Awareness at the Zero Day Initiative (ZDI), said. "Is AI to blame? Partly. It's accelerating bug-hunting on both sides of the fence, so vendors are finding (and fixing) more flaws, and researchers are finding them faster too."
"But AI isn't creating these bugs out of thin air; it's just shortening the time between a vulnerability existing and someone noticing it. The volume isn't the real story anymore. What matters is that discovery is scaling faster than exploitation, so teams that triage by sheer CVE count instead of exploitability are burning cycles on the wrong bugs. Patch what's proven, prioritized, and public, and treat everything else as this month's new normal."

Google empezó a permitir que cualquier persona con una cuenta instale en su propio celular Android aplicaciones creadas con inteligencia artificial, sin pasar por el proceso de publicación en la tienda Play Store. La función, llamada “biblioteca personal”, se activa a partir de este martes en Estados Unidos y otros mercados seleccionados, para mayores de 18 años.
La novedad apunta a quienes usan Google AI Studio, la herramienta de la compañía para generar aplicaciones a partir de instrucciones escritas en lenguaje cotidiano, una práctica conocida como vibe coding (programar describiendo lo que uno quiere, sin escribir código).
Hasta ahora, para correr esas aplicaciones en un teléfono Android había que conectar el dispositivo a una computadora o publicarlas en la tienda, con lo cual quedaban disponibles para los cerca de 3.000 millones de usuarios de Play Store.
Cómo funciona la biblioteca personal
Con el cambio, la aplicación generada se guarda en una sección exclusiva del perfil del usuario y no aparece en las búsquedas, los listados ni las recomendaciones de la tienda. Solo la persona que la creó puede instalarla, y puede hacerlo en varios de sus dispositivos con acceso a Play.
“Esa es la razón por la que el futuro de las aplicaciones en Google Play es personal, seguro y hecho por todos”, afirmó Sam Bright, vicepresidente y gerente general de Google Play y el Ecosistema de Desarrolladores, en una conferencia de prensa previa al anuncio, citado por TechCrunch.

articles.title: Un juez ordenó a OpenAI entregarle a Apple sus registros de contratación por el juicio de secretos comerciales

El fallo, firmado por el juez Edward Davila, del tribunal federal del distrito norte de California, obliga a OpenAI a presentar documentos de las entrevistas realizadas a esos exempleados de Apple que aplicaron a sus grupos de hardware de consumo y robótica.
La orden fija un plazo de cinco días para los materiales que OpenAI ya había recopilado durante el litigio, y de 14 días para el resto de los documentos. Entre ellos figuran guías de entrevista, instructivos, guiones y presentaciones técnicas que podrían mencionar tecnología de Apple.
Davila también autorizó a Apple a revisar mensajes privados enviados por la aplicación LINE entre empleados de OpenAI nombrados en la causa, Chang Liu y Yu-Ting Peng, conocida como Alyssa Peng, desde enero de 2026.
El juez además aprobó las declaraciones bajo juramento de ambos y de Tang Yew Tan, jefe de hardware de OpenAI, que al igual que sus colegas trabajó antes en Apple.
Apple presentó la demanda el 10 de julio y acusa a sus extrabajadores de un patrón de robo de información confidencial. Según la compañía, usaron computadoras de Apple para descargar archivos con datos sobre tecnologías y productos no anunciados.

articles.title: Google Play Protect: truco gratis para analizar tu móvil y eliminar malware en segundos

Google Play Protect permite analizar gratis un móvil Android para detectar malware y aplicaciones potencialmente dañinas. La herramienta viene integrada en Google Play Store, revisa los programas descargados desde la tienda oficial y también examina aplicaciones instaladas desde otras fuentes. Si identifica un riesgo, puede enviar una alerta, impedir la instalación, inhabilitar el programa o eliminarlo del dispositivo.
Play Protect actúa como una capa de seguridad que funciona de forma predeterminada en Android y ayuda a identificar comportamientos sospechosos antes de que una aplicación acceda a datos personales, permisos sensibles o funciones del teléfono.
Cómo analizar un móvil Android con Google Play Protect
El proceso para revisar si hay aplicaciones peligrosas es gratuito y se realiza desde Google Play Store. No es necesario instalar un antivirus adicional para utilizar esta función, aunque la herramienta no sustituye hábitos básicos de seguridad, como evitar descargas desde fuentes desconocidas.
Para comprobar el estado de protección, hay que seguir estos pasos:
- Abrir la aplicación Google Play Store en el móvil.
- Pulsar el icono de perfil, situado en la esquina superior derecha.
- Seleccionar la opción Play Protect.
- Revisar el resultado del análisis o tocar el botón de exploración si aparece disponible.
- Consultar las alertas sobre aplicaciones potencialmente dañinas.
